artigo.texto: Canadian Solar Inc. has announced that its energy storage solutions business, e-STORAGE, has signed an agreement to supply and commission a 100 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for OX2’s Muswellbrook Solar Farm and Battery project in New South Wales, Australia. Shipments for the project are scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, while commercial operations are targeted for the third quarter of 2028. The battery cells and SolBank systems will be manufactured at Canadian Solar’s own facilities, providing greater supply-chain visibility and quality control. Under the agreement, e-STORAGE will deliver an integrated energy storage solution based on its SolBank 3.0 battery containers, along with power conversion systems, plant controls and its proprietary EQ-S Energy Management System (EMS). The EMS has been developed in-house by e-STORAGE’s North American software team. The company will also undertake R1 grid connection studies, provide a hybrid power plant controller to coordinate the battery system with the co-located solar farm, and lead the overall integration and commissioning of the hybrid facility. The project is backed by a 20-year long-term service agreement (LTSA), covering hardware, proprietary software and long-term system performance under a single service arrangement. Located approximately 2.5 kilometres east of Muswellbrook, the solar-plus-storage facility will be developed on land at a former coal mine within the Hunter-Central Coast Renewable Energy Zone. The project comes as the Hunter region prepares for the retirement of aging coal-fired generation capacity in the early 2030s. The two-hour battery system is expected to store surplus solar generation during periods of high daytime output and dispatch electricity during evening peak-demand periods, supporting grid reliability as conventional thermal generation declines. Once operational, the BESS will support OX2’s long-term hybrid power purchase agreement for the project. By combining solar generation with dispatchable battery storage, the facility is designed to provide firmer renewable electricity while supporting the Hunter region’s transition away from coal-fired power. Steve Symons, Vice President of OX2 Australia, said the storage system would transform Muswellbrook into a hybrid facility capable of capturing solar power when available and supplying it when required by the grid. Jeff Roy, President of e-STORAGE, highlighted the growing role of battery storage in regions transitioning away from coal generation, adding that e-STORAGE’s integrated approach covers battery cells, energy management software and long-term servicing. artigo.texto: OS DATA CENTERS CRESCEM DE IMPORTÂNCIA E JÁ SERÃO TEMA DE UM DEBATE INTERNACIONAL QUE COMEÇA AMANHÃ EM SÃO PAULO A primeira edição do Data Center World Brasil começa amanhã (6), no São Paulo Expo, em um momento em que decisões sobre energia, tributação, conectividade e capacidade computacional ganham peso na definição de onde e como serão instalados os próximos grandes projetos de data centers no país. A programação reúne debates sobre condições regulatórias, investimentos, disponibilidade de energia, conectividade, refrigeração, operação e capacidade computacional, diante de uma nova geração de aplicações de inteligência artificial que exige infraestruturas mais robustas e eficientes. Um dos temas que chegam ao congresso é o Redata, novo regime especial de tributação para serviços de data center, criado para estimular investimentos no setor. A medida será discutida às 10h30, na Opening Arena, durante o painel “Infraestrutura digital como ativo geopolítico: competitividade, investimentos, regulação e o que precisa mudar”. A conversa aborda os efeitos do programa sobre a atração de investimentos, a competitividade do país e as decisões que podem influenciar a infraestrutura digital nos próximos cinco a dez anos. O debate passa ainda pelo impacto do Confaz e do ICMS sobre a competitividade do setor. A energia é outro fator decisivo nessa equação. O avanço da inteligência artificial elevou a demanda por capacidade computacional e trouxe novos desafios para a implantação e a operação dos data centers. Localização, disponibilidade energética, eficiência e continuidade operacional estão entre os temas que atravessam a programação do congresso Na sequência, às 11h30, a roundtable “Energia como gargalo estrutural: disponibilidade, intermitência e viabilidade real” discute a oferta efetiva de energia, modelos de geração, armazenamento e alternativas para garantir estabilidade às operações. Às 14h, o painel “Como grandes empresas escolhem data centers na prática: decisões reais de custo, risco e performance” traz a perspectiva de quem utiliza essa infraestrutura e precisa equilibrar localização, latência, custo, segurança e continuidade dos serviços. A discussão sobre investimentos volta às 16h, com a roundtable “Financiamento, viabilidade e expansão: por que projetos travam — e como viabilizar na prática”, que reúne representantes do Ministério das Comunicações, BNDES, Brasscom e Patria Investments. O debate aborda capital, crédito e as condições necessárias para tirar grandes projetos do papel. A conectividade também ganha espaço entre os assuntos que ajudam a explicar a expansão do setor. O avanço das redes de alta capacidade reforça a importância de conexões estratégicas para sustentar data centers, serviços de cloud e aplicações digitais cada vez mais intensivas em processamento. No dia 7, quarta-feira, o painel “Latência, rotas globais e edge: onde a infraestrutura decide o jogo”, às 10h30, aborda a relação entre localização, conectividade e desempenho. Às 15h15, o painel “Desafios dos Hyperscalers: como planejar capacidade em um mercado imprevisível” coloca no centro da conversa o desafio de ampliar a capacidade diante do crescimento da demanda impulsionada pela IA. Logo depois, às 16h, o estudo de caso “Continuidade operacional em data centers: como se preparar para falhas, crises e eventos extremos” contempla estratégias de preparação para situações capazes de afetar as operações. Para fechar o segundo dia, às 16h30, o LATAM Leaders Panel “Data centers na América Latina: investimento, expansão e decisões de arquitetura” amplia a discussão para os movimentos de investimento e crescimento do mercado regional. A inteligência artificial ganha ainda mais espaço no último dia do congresso. Na quinta-feira, 8 de outubro, às 10h30, o C-Level Panel “Expansão na era da IA: decisões que definem bilhões em investimento” discute escolhas de infraestrutura, energia e capacidade diante da nova escala de demanda. Às 14h, o painel “Data centers AI-ready: densidade, energia e novos requisitos de infraestrutura” mostra como cargas computacionais mais intensivas estão mudando a arquitetura dos empreendimentos. O aumento da densidade dos racks pressiona sistemas elétricos e térmicos e acelera a adoção de tecnologias de refrigeração mais eficientes, como o liquid cooling. Para Leonardo Benedicto, diretor do Data Center World Brasil, a transformação provocada pela IA exige que o setor olhe para os data centers de forma mais ampla. “A inteligência artificial está mudando rapidamente a forma como pensamos os data centers. Não é apenas uma questão de aumentar capacidade. É preciso considerar energia, refrigeração, espaço e a possibilidade de ampliar as instalações ao longo do tempo. O desafio é construir uma infraestrutura que acompanhe a velocidade dessa transformação e esteja preparada para as demandas que ainda estão por vir.” A expansão do setor também tem reflexos sobre a economia. Estudo da FGV aponta que 100 MW de capacidade instalada em data centers podem representar cerca de 12,5 mil empregos, evidenciando o alcance dos investimentos em infraestrutura digital para além do mercado de tecnologia.

artigo.texto: Verlume conclui testes hiperbáricos de sistema de bateria submarina de 500 kWh antes de implantação no Mar do Norte holandês A Verlume, especialista em baterias submarinas e sistemas de gerenciamento de energia com sede no Reino Unido, testou seu sistema modular de armazenamento de energia submarino de 500 kWh em Aberdeen antes de uma implantação planejada no Mar do Norte holandês, de acordo com a Offshore Energy. O sistema está previsto para se tornar a primeira bateria submarina formadora de rede co-localizada com energia eólica offshore após a instalação. A Verlume informou em 1º de outubro que havia concluído os testes hiperbáricos de seu invólucro submarino Orah na instalação de testes hiperbáricos da JFD em Aberdeen, um passo que a empresa descreveu como um importante marco de qualificação antes da implantação planejada do sistema no parque eólico offshore OranjeWind. Esse projeto está sendo desenvolvido pela RWE e pela TotalEnergies na costa holandesa. O sistema modular de armazenamento de energia submarino de 500 kWh foi projetado para fornecer suporte autônomo de rede para parques eólicos offshore. O Orah utiliza química de bateria atual e é gerenciado pela plataforma de gerenciamento de energia Axonn da Verlume. Segundo a empresa, essas tecnologias se combinam para formar uma solução modular de armazenamento de energia e suporte autônomo de rede destinada a ajudar a viabilizar sistemas de energia offshore mais flexíveis e resilientes. Com peso de 10 toneladas e dimensões de 7,2 metros de comprimento, 2,4 metros de largura e 2,4 metros de altura, o sistema é descrito como o maior vaso já testado no centro hiperbárico da JFD até o momento. O programa de testes submeteu o invólucro a um perfil de pressão controlado que representa seu ambiente operacional submarino pretendido. Ele se concentrou em três áreas críticas: qualificação de pressão e profundidade, integridade do invólucro e desempenho funcional sob pressão. Depois que o sistema completo de 85 toneladas for implantado no parque eólico offshore OranjeWind, ele representará a primeira bateria submarina formadora de rede co-localizada com energia eólica offshore. artigo.texto: Calgon Carbon Corporation A Kuraray company, global leader in specialty carbons. According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Impregnated Activated Carbon market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global impregnated activated carbon market is entering a phase of sustained expansion, with demand projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 5–7% between 2026 and 2035. This specialized segment of the activated carbon industry is distinguished by chemically treated carbons that selectively remove specific contaminants—such as mercury, hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, and volatile organic compounds—from gas and liquid streams. Unlike commodity activated carbon, impregnated grades command significant price premiums, often 100–200% above standard products, reflecting their engineered performance and the critical nature of their applications. The market is being reshaped by tightening environmental regulations, particularly in North America and Europe, where mercury emission limits for coal-fired power plants and industrial boilers are driving adoption. Simultaneously, the rapid expansion of biogas and renewable natural gas projects is creating new demand for impregnated carbons used in desulfurization. Food and feed processing industries are also increasingly specifying these carbons to meet stringent safety and quality standards. Supply remains concentrated among a dozen global producers, with most national markets dependent on imports. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the market size, segmentation, competitive landscape, and regional dynamics, offering a data-driven outlook to 2035. The baseline scenario for the impregnated activated carbon market anticipates a 5–7% CAGR from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching approximately 180 (2025=100) by the end of the forecast period. This growth is underpinned by regulatory mandates rather than discretionary spending, providing a high degree of demand visibility. In North America and Europe, mercury and air toxics standards (MATS) and the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) are compelling utilities and industrial operators to install or upgrade injection and fixed-bed systems using brominated or sulfur-impregnated carbons. In Asia-Pacific, while regulations are less uniform, China's ultra-low emission standards for coal-fired power and India's tightening environmental norms are creating substantial incremental demand. The biogas sector, supported by renewable energy incentives in Europe and North America, represents the fastest-growing application, with desulfurization requirements driving double-digit growth in that niche. Food and feed processing applications are also expanding, as clean-label trends and food safety regulations push processors to adopt impregnated carbons for purification. On the supply side, capacity expansions are underway in China and Southeast Asia, but qualification cycles for regulated applications remain lengthy, limiting supply elasticity. Raw material price volatility—particularly for coal-based and coconut shell precursors—poses a risk to margins, though producers have demonstrated some ability to pass through costs. Overall, the market is expected to remain tight for high-purity, certified grades, with contract-based procurement becoming the norm. The air and gas purification segment is the largest end-use sector for impregnated activated carbon, accounting for an estimated 35% of global demand. This segment is primarily driven by the need to remove mercury, dioxins, and acid gases from flue gas streams in coal-fired power plants, waste incinerators, and industrial boilers. In North America and Europe, regulations such as the Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) and the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) mandate strict emission limits, compelling operators to adopt brominated or sulfur-impregnated carbons for mercury capture. Through 2035, demand in this segment is expected to grow at a moderate pace in developed markets as retrofits are completed, but accelerate in Asia-Pacific where China and India are tightening emission standards. Key demand-side indicators include coal-fired power generation capacity, waste incineration rates, and regulatory enforcement timelines. The segment is also seeing innovation in multi-pollutant control, where impregnated carbons are formulated to simultaneously capture mercury, SO2, and NOx, offering cost advantages. However, the long-term outlook is tempered by the gradual retirement of coal plants in some regions, offset by growth in waste-to-energy and industrial processes. Current trend: Growing due to mercury and air toxics regulations. Major trends: Increasing adoption of brominated activated carbon for mercury removal in coal-fired power plants, Development of multi-functional carbons for simultaneous removal of multiple pollutants, Growth in waste-to-energy capacity driving demand for dioxin removal, and Retrofitting of older industrial boilers with activated carbon injection systems. Representative participants: Cabot Corporation, Calgon Carbon Corporation, Jacobi Carbons, Haycarb PLC, and Donau Carbon GmbH. Water treatment represents approximately 25% of global impregnated activated carbon demand, encompassing municipal drinking water, industrial process water, and wastewater treatment. Impregnated carbons are used to remove specific contaminants such as hydrogen sulfide, chlorine, chloramines, and heavy metals like arsenic and lead. In municipal drinking water, regulations such as the U.S. Safe Drinking Water Act and the EU Drinking Water Directive are driving adoption, particularly for the removal of emerging contaminants like PFAS and pesticides. artigo.texto: The Alabama Public Service Commission voted on Tuesday to keep a ‘deemed approved’ process that lets Alabama Power’s electricity contracts with the largest data centers take effect without a vote of the commission. The new rule extends the review period from 10 days to 90 days, but retains the previous rule of automatic approval for Alabama Power data center contracts if the commission fails to make a decision within 90 days. Energy Alabama advocated for a public vote on all applicable data center contracts in written comments this summer. “For three decades, rules built for manufacturers let contracts take effect without a vote of the Commission. Data centers on this scale are a different animal,” Daniel Tait, executive director of Energy Alabama, said. “Ninety days is better than ten, but silence still counts as yes. A contract this big should never take effect because nobody voted. Alabamians deserve to see their regulators decide, in public.” The Alabama Attorney General's Office also submitted comments on August 6, calling for a vote by commission members on contracts between Alabama Power and data centers. “The elected and appointed members of the Alabama Public Service Commission must actively participate in the decisions of the commission by voting on large load contracts, especially when the matter involves an assessment of public benefits or a determination of the public interest,” Olivia Martin, division chief of consumer interest with the AG’s Office, said in August. The new rule requires Alabama Power to file a public petition naming the data center customer and its parent companies, the city or county where the facility will be built, and the maximum amount of power it has contracted for. Other aspects of the contract would be confidential. All three members of the commission said they wanted future commissioners to vote on the contracts, but still approved a “deemed approved” process where contracts could be approved if the commission doesn’t vote within 90 days of the petition being submitted. According to the rule approved at Tuesday’s meeting, “Contracts submitted under this process shall be approved or disapproved through a commission vote within 90 days of the submission of the filing of the petition. If the commission fails to vote within 90 days, the petition is deemed approved.” “I feel strongly that we should take a public vote as a commission on data centers. We should not follow the deemed approved process that we’ve been following for a number of years,” Cynthia Almond, Public Service Commission President, said. “It should be a very public process we go through, I believe, because the public is very interested in this, very concerned about it. If we don’t take a public vote, that to me is not doing our job.” Almond and other commission members, Jeremy Oden and Chip Beeker, also voted for the new rule. Oden and Beeker both lost their Republican primary races in May. The commission is set to expand to seven seats in January 2027 under a new law passed in the 2026 session. artigo.texto: CATL Partners With BME: What It Means for Contemporary Amperex Technology stock Published on 10/04/2026 at 17:35 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited signed a cooperation agreement with BME on September 16, 2026, to support battery-pack assembly and production in Egypt, according to the company’s announcement. Egyptian battery-pack manufacturing Under the agreement, BME plans to source battery cells from CATL. CATL will provide battery-pack technology licensing, production equipment and technical training. BME is an Egyptian battery manufacturer, and the planned facility is intended to assemble and produce battery packs for heavy-duty commercial vehicles. Planned capacity The facility, which BME is developing and fully funding, is planned to have an initial annual production capacity of 1 GWh. BME’s longer-term plan calls for annual capacity to expand to 5 GWh and for the product range to include passenger-vehicle battery packs and energy-storage systems. These details were reported in CATL’s company release. Commercial-vehicle technology In a separate September 14, 2026 release, CATL said it unveiled its TECTRANS II commercial-vehicle battery platform at IAA Transportation 2026 in Hanover. The company said the platform supports configurations with a maximum driving range of up to 1,000 kilometers and 80% charging in 25 minutes with megawatt-level fast charging, according to PR Newswire.

artigo.texto: • 13 min de lectura Até 30 de setembro de 2026, as empresas de transporte marítimo devem entregar as Licenças de Emissão da UE (EUAs) que cubram 70% das suas emissões verificadas e abrangidas a partir de 2025. A nossa equipa de Mercados de Carbono está aqui para o ajudar a compreender a sua posição e a preparar-se para o prazo, quer já tenha negociado EUAs connosco, seja um cliente nosso de energia marítima, esteja a comprar EUAs pela primeira vez ou precise de apoio para cumprir a sua obrigação regulamentar. Os preços dos EUAs respondem a mudanças na oferta, procura, política e no mercado de energia em geral. Ter uma visão clara dos seus requisitos esperados dá-lhe maior flexibilidade para considerar quando e como comprar, enquanto gere o seu orçamento e obrigações de conformidade. Os EUAs são uma parte cada vez mais importante da estratégia mais ampla de combustível e conformidade de um armador, o requisito de entrega aumentará para 100% das emissões em 2026, tornando-se não apenas uma transação anual. A KPI OceanConnect combina a experiência no mercado de carbono com uma compreensão da sua aquisição de combustível, operações e exposição regulamentar mais ampla. Isso permite-nos ajudá-lo a considerar as suas compras de EUA no contexto da sua estratégia geral de energia marítima. Clientes de EUA que regressam Reveja a sua posição de emissões de 2025, avalie quaisquer requisitos de EUA restantes e desenvolva a estratégia já em vigor. Clientes existentes de combustível marítimo Aproxime as suas estratégias de aquisição de combustível e EUA, apoiado por um parceiro com experiência em ambos os mercados. Novos clientes de EUA Obtenha uma visão clara dos volumes de EUA de que necessita, das opções de compra disponíveis e dos passos a seguir até à entrega. Empresas sem recursos dedicados ao EU ETS Aceda a suporte dedicado ao mercado de carbono sem a necessidade de uma equipa interna de conformidade ou negociação. Trabalhamos em conjunto com a sua equipa para calcular os requisitos e planear as compras, apoiar as transferências e facilitar o processo de entrega. A nossa equipa de Combustíveis Alternativos e Mercados de Carbono pode ajudá-lo a: A KPI OceanConnect apoia mais de 250 clientes com os seus requisitos de carbono e conformidade e negociou mais de 4,5 milhões de EUAs. Os nossos especialistas em mercado de carbono trabalham em conjunto com as nossas equipas globais de combustível marítimo, combinando conhecimento regulamentar, inteligência de mercado e décadas de experiência na negociação de energia marítima. Isso dá-lhe continuidade na aquisição de combustível, EU ETS e no cenário de transição energética em desenvolvimento. Quer precise de cumprir os requisitos deste ano ou desenvolver uma estratégia de compra a longo prazo, podemos fornecer o nível de suporte que se adapta à sua frota e organização. Para armadores e operadores cujos navios escalam portos da UE e do EEE, as obrigações do Sistema de Comércio de Emissões da União Europeia (EU ETS) e do FuelEU Maritime estão cada vez mais interligadas com as estratégias de aquisição de combustível. O combustível que queima molda a sua exposição ao carbono, e a sua estratégia de carbono molda qual combustível faz sentido comercial. Gerir múltiplas prioridades requer a compreensão dos riscos e oportunidades em jogo. Este FAQ aborda as perguntas que mais ouvimos dos operadores que tentam juntar estas peças numa estratégia coerente e económica. Sim. O combustível que escolhe abastecer tem um impacto direto no volume de EUAs que precisa de entregar, porque a sua obrigação de EUA é calculada a partir das emissões verificadas do seu navio. Combustíveis com menor teor de carbono, como biocombustíveis sustentáveis qualificados, podem reduzir esse valor de emissões, o que, por sua vez, reduz o número de EUAs que precisa de entregar. Em certos locais e momentos, a diferença de preço entre biocombustíveis e combustíveis convencionais diminuiu significativamente e, uma vez incluídos os custos de conformidade, a comparação do custo total pode favorecer o combustível alternativo. Isso destaca como a escolha do combustível agora precisa ser uma decisão mais ponderada, considerando tanto a conformidade quanto os custos. Isso é particularmente relevante porque a fase de implementação do EU ETS atinge 100% para as emissões geradas em 2026, com as licenças correspondentes a serem entregues em 2027. As emissões de metano e óxido nitroso também entram no esquema a partir de 2026, aumentando ainda mais a importância de cada decisão de combustível. Tomar decisões de combustível e EUA isoladamente corre o risco de incorrer numa fatura de conformidade mais alta do que o necessário. Ao avaliar as opções de combustível juntamente com os seus custos ajustados à conformidade, os operadores podem identificar onde uma mudança no tipo de combustível pode reduzir o custo total da viagem, mesmo que o próprio combustível tenha um preço diferente no papel. O EU ETS e o FuelEU Maritime são estruturas regulamentares separadas que podem aplicar-se ao mesmo navio, mas operam de forma diferente. O EU ETS é um mecanismo de precificação de carbono sob o qual as empresas de transporte marítimo devem entregar EUAs correspondentes às suas emissões verificadas e abrangidas. O requisito cobre 70% das emissões geradas em 2025 e cobrirá 100% das emissões geradas a partir de 2026. O FuelEU Maritime, por outro lado, estabelece limites progressivamente mais rigorosos para a intensidade de gases de efeito estufa do poço ao navio da energia utilizada a bordo, e para cumprir, os armadores precisarão de abastecer combustíveis mais limpos. A conformidade também pode ser alcançada através de acordos de pool, que permitem que o saldo positivo de conformidade de um navio compense o défice de outro. Na prática, isso significa que uma única decisão de combustível ou operacional pode afetar a sua posição em ambas as regulamentações. artigo.texto: CATL, Sungrow, Tesla and BYD are leading the global battery energy storage system market in 2026, but their leadership differs significantly across battery shipments, system integration, software, regional market share and mega-project execution. Battery storage has become one of the fastest-growing parts of global power infrastructure as utilities add batteries to integrate solar and wind, manage peak demand, provide grid flexibility and improve energy security. Global battery storage additions reached 108 GW in 2025, up 40 percent, according to the International Energy Agency. Installed capacity is now 11 times higher than in 2021. Around 80 percent of new capacity was utility-scale, while lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, accounted for approximately 90 percent of deployments. China represented around 60 percent of global additions, followed by the United States and Europe. Growth accelerated further in 2026. SNE Research reported global lithium-ion ESS battery shipments of 461.3 GWh in H1 2026, up 71 percent from 269.7 GWh a year earlier. Markets outside China accounted for 258.7 GWh, or 56 percent, exceeding half of global shipments for the first time. The global battery storage market is therefore moving rapidly beyond China, even though Chinese manufacturers continue to dominate battery-cell production and system integration. Which Company Is the World’s Largest Battery Storage Supplier? There is no single answer because the industry uses different measurements. CATL is the world’s largest ESS battery-cell supplier by H1 2026 shipments, delivering 125 GWh and capturing 27.1 percent of the global market. Sungrow ranks first in Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 Global BESS Integrator Comprehensive Ranking, which evaluates companies across technology, safety, R&D, supply chains, vertical integration, financial strength and other criteria. Tesla remains particularly strong in North America, while BYD combines cell manufacturing, system integration and large-scale project execution. The distinction matters because battery-cell manufacturing and BESS integration are different businesses. Global Top 10 Battery Storage Companies in 2026 Wood Mackenzie’s comprehensive 2026 BESS integrator ranking places the companies in the following order: The ranking demonstrates why BESS procurement is moving beyond battery price toward efficiency, safety, financial strength and lifetime performance. 1. Sungrow: World’s Top BESS Integrator Sungrow ranks first in Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 comprehensive assessment. Its advantage comes from combining battery systems with power conversion systems, controls and global project-integration capabilities. That is important because PCS efficiency, thermal management, grid-forming capability and system controls directly affect lifetime project economics. Sungrow also leads Europe’s BESS integrator market and has established a particularly strong position in the Middle East. 2. Tesla: Megapack and Software Create a Different Model Tesla ranks second globally in the comprehensive assessment and remains the leading BESS integrator in North America. Its Megapack strategy combines utility-scale battery hardware with Autobidder software, which can optimize battery participation in electricity markets. Tesla’s strength demonstrates why the storage battle extends beyond battery chemistry. Software capable of determining when to charge, discharge and participate in energy or ancillary-services markets can directly influence project revenue. 3. CATL: 125 GWh Makes It the ESS Battery-Cell Leader CATL dominates when measured by battery-cell shipments. The company shipped 125 GWh of ESS batteries during H1 2026, up 81 percent year over year, increasing its market share from 25.6 percent to 27.1 percent. For comparison, second-ranked EVE Energy shipped 48 GWh, while Hithium delivered 46.2 GWh. CATL therefore shipped more ESS batteries than the next two suppliers individually by a very wide margin. Its huge LFP manufacturing scale provides significant cost advantages, while continued investment in alternative technologies including sodium-ion could broaden its future storage portfolio. 4. BYD: Vertical Integration Meets Mega-Scale Storage BYD combines battery-cell manufacturing, electronics and complete storage-system integration. Its H1 2026 ESS cell shipments reached 35.7 GWh, giving it 7.7 percent global share. Its project footprint is equally important. BYD’s total contracted battery volume with Grenergy for Chile’s Oasis de Atacama project has reached 6.5 GWh across project phases. BYD is also gaining ground in Europe, where it moved from fifth to second among integrators. In the Middle East, BYD and Sungrow together captured 87 percent of the BESS market in 2025, demonstrating the scale of Chinese supplier expansion. 5. Envision Energy: Combining Renewables, Storage and Digital Control Envision and Trina Storage share fifth position in Wood Mackenzie’s comprehensive global ranking. Envision’s strategy extends beyond batteries because the company participates across renewable generation, storage and digital energy management. It ranked third in Asia-Pacific behind CRRC and HyperStrong. Combining wind, solar, storage and digital optimization could become valuable as utilities move toward integrated renewable-energy projects rather than procuring individual technologies separately. 6. Trina Storage: Utility-Scale Integration Trina Storage has developed its BESS position around the Elementa platform and utility-scale LFP projects. The company’s integration with the broader Trina Solar ecosystem also creates opportunities in solar-plus-storage. For developers, greater system density can reduce land requirements and some balance-of-system costs, while integrated battery and power-electronics design can improve project efficiency. 7. artigo.texto: Mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V até 2035: crescimento se acelera com a demanda de data centers e renováveis Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V, o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano até 2035. Esse crescimento se apoia em três forças estruturais: a rápida expansão de data centers e de projetos de escala utilitária, a integração de energias renováveis e de sistemas de armazenamento em baterias e a eletrificação industrial em curso. A Ásia-Pacífico segue como centro de gravidade tanto da produção quanto do consumo, respondendo por quase metade da produção mundial e por parcela semelhante da demanda. As cadeias de suprimento regionais, porém, estão se redesenhando, com fabricantes ampliando capacidade de montagem na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para reduzir prazos de entrega e atender a exigências de conteúdo local. O mercado também passa por uma atualização tecnológica: painéis de distribuição inteligentes, com medição integrada, proteção contra arco elétrico e monitoramento remoto, conquistam participação crescente em projetos de grande porte e alcançam prêmios de preço de 30–60% sobre as configurações básicas. Ao mesmo tempo, a volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas e os prazos prolongados de componentes representam riscos para margens e fornecimento. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, arquitetura da demanda, dinâmica competitiva e tendências regionais até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V prevê crescimento constante até 2035, com a demanda global avançando a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano. Essa projeção pressupõe continuidade dos investimentos em infraestrutura de rede, projetos de energia renovável e data centers, além de despesas de capital industrial moderadas. A Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo o maior mercado, sustentada por polos manufatureiros na China, na Índia e no Sudeste Asiático, mas o crescimento também se acelerará na América do Norte e na Europa, à medida que a infraestrutura envelhecida for modernizada e a digitalização das redes de baixa tensão ganhar ritmo. O índice de mercado (2025=100) deve alcançar 185 em 2035, refletindo uma quase duplicação da atividade de mercado no período de previsão. Entre as principais incertezas estão a volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas, sobretudo cobre e aço, e o ritmo de harmonização das normas entre as regiões. Ainda assim, os vetores fundamentais da demanda — eletrificação, descarbonização e digitalização — são robustos, e espera-se que o mercado supere o crescimento industrial mais amplo. A migração para equipamentos de distribuição inteligentes continuará a remodelar portfólios de produtos e posicionamento competitivo, com ganho de participação para fornecedores capazes de oferecer soluções integradas, em conformidade com as normas e com entrega rápida. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Expansão acelerada de data centers e infraestrutura de nuvem, que exige distribuição de energia 380V/400V confiável para servidores, refrigeração e sistemas de backup. - Integração de energias renováveis e armazenamento em baterias, em que usinas solares e eólicas precisam de distribuição CA de baixa tensão dedicada para inversores e cargas auxiliares. - Eletrificação e automação industrial, com fábricas migrando para a manufatura inteligente e substituindo processos a combustível fóssil por alternativas elétricas. - Investimentos em modernização e resiliência da rede, sobretudo na América do Norte e na Europa, para substituir equipamentos envelhecidos e melhorar a confiabilidade. - Digitalização da distribuição de baixa tensão, com disjuntores e sistemas de monitoramento habilitados para IoT especificados em 20–30% dos grandes projetos. - Regionalização das cadeias de suprimento, levando fabricantes a estabelecer montagem local na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para atender às regras de conteúdo local. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas, especialmente cobre e aço galvanizado, que pressiona margens e complica licitações de preço fixo. - Prazos prolongados para componentes especializados, como disjuntores em caixa moldada, limitando a produção de integradores de pequeno e médio porte. - Divergências de normas de segurança e desempenho entre regiões (IEC, UL, AS/NZS), elevando os custos de qualificação para fornecedores globais. - Escassez de mão de obra qualificada para instalação e comissionamento, sobretudo em projetos de renováveis e data centers em rápido crescimento. - Concorrência intensa de produtores de baixo custo, especialmente nos segmentos de linha padrão, limitando o poder de precificação dos fornecedores premium. Estrutura da demanda por indústria de uso final Infraestrutura de rede (participação estimada: 30%) A infraestrutura de rede continua sendo o maior setor de uso final da distribuição de energia 380V/400V, respondendo por cerca de 30% da demanda global. Esse segmento abrange subestações de transmissão e distribuição, postes de derivação e quadros de baixa tensão que conectam redes de média tensão aos usuários finais. artigo.texto: Atmos Renewables, an Australian renewableenergy firm, has reached financial close on two Capacity Investment Scheme-backed projects in Australia: the 400 MW/1,600 MWh Teebar BESS and 470 MW Parron Maam Marang Wind Farm. Atmos Renewables is the Australian renewable energy business of Igneo Infrastructure Partners, developing, owning and operating utility-scale wind, solar and battery storage assets. The four-hour Teebar BESS will be built beside Powerlink’s Teebar Creek substation in Queensland’s Fraser Coast region. Parron Maam Marang will be developed in Western Australia’s Wheatbelt and supply electricity to Synergy under a long-term PPA. Together with the 100 MW/400 MWh Merredin BESS, Atmos has taken 970 MW of CIS-backed capacity through financial close over 16 months. Atmos will retain ownership of both projects during construction and operate them after completion. Its national portfolio now exceeds 1.5 GW of operating and under-construction wind, solar and storage capacity. Atmos closes financing for 400 MW Teebar BESS, wind farm Atmos Renewables reached financial close on 870 MW of CIS-backed battery and wind projects in Queensland and Western Australia, expanding its portfolio. artigo.texto: A Plattsburgh man planned a data center in Chateaugay. Locals are pushing back The rumors started swirling a few months ago. Chateaugay, a small farming town in northern Franklin County, may soon get a data center. But little was known about the project, including who was behind it and what stage of development the data center was in. Chateaugay joins a growing list of towns across the country that developers are eyeing as demand for data processing sites grows amid the artificial intelligence boom. Last Monday evening, dozens of people showed up at the Chateaugay town board meeting looking for answers about the potential project. Turnout was so much higher than normal that the meeting was moved to a larger room. Paula King, who lives in Chateaugay, was among those who expressed some skepticism about the project. "I am all for local development, but I like to be sure that we’re mitigating any harm to the environment, to the people that live within the communities and that we maximize benefits from this," said King. Details of the proposed project The property where the potential data center would be built is a few miles south of downtown Chateaugay. The 19-acre property is the site of a former wood chip factory. In 2022, Joseph Church from Plattsburgh purchased the property for $500,000. Church is a veterinarian and a former partner at the Plattsburgh Animal Hospital, where he worked for more than two decades. According to his LinkedIn, Church is also the founder and CEO of New York GreenCloud, a company focused on "developing data center infrastructure powered by renewable energy.” A year after he bought the property, Church presented his data center proposal to the Chateaugay town board. According to his company's website, the data center could consume up to 15 megawatts of power, which is much smaller than the project currently under review in nearby Massena, which would be designed for 635 megawatts. Developer of the site in Chateaugay faces problems When it was first proposed, Chateaugay Town Supervisor Don Bilow said he was open to it. "When they presented the project, it looked like a nice project, but now we’re starting to get doubts about it," said Bilow after last week's meeting. Bilow said he hasn’t heard anything from Church in three years. Church also did not respond to multiple requests for comment for this article. Along with the site in Chateaugay, Church is also planning to build a data center at the Buena Vista biomass plant in Amador County, California. A local newspaper reporter from the Ledger Dispatch in northern California interviewed Church earlier this spring and asked about the project in Chateaugay. Despite it being listed as "in construction" on his company's website, Church admitted that the project has been stalled. "The problem with Chateaugay- it’s not abandoned due to any issues; it's that the site is not in the condition that Buena Vista was in," said Church. There was some work done on the site in Chateaugay a few years ago. Church hired an electrical company from Clinton County, but according to public court records, he never paid the company, so they sued. A judge ordered Church to pay back more than $38,000. In recent years, he has also been sued by two credit card companies over unpaid debt. In those two cases, Church was ordered to pay back a combined $54,000. Skepticism and fears arise over the proposed data center When he was interviewed earlier this spring, Church said he was still hopeful his business will take off, and he claimed that the community in Chateaugay was supportive of his project. "Chateaugay welcomes the restart of that place," said Church, later adding that "they would love to see it come back." But that’s not an accurate reflection of the local sentiment now that more people are aware of the project. According to some who were at Chateaugay’s town board meeting last week, most commenters were either skeptical of the data center or against it. "I fear that there’s too much unknown with what a data center is actually capable of," said Cecilia Merrill. Her top concern is about the environmental impact of a data center. Along with requiring a lot of power, data centers also need a lot of cooling capacity. The property Church owns is about 1,000 ft. from the Chateaugay River, where Merrill goes fishing about five times a week. "The brook trout in it are still thriving; they’re beautiful," said Merrill. "There’s wild fish in there, and there’s a color pink on some of them that I’ve never seen on any other spectrum of light.” She’s worried all that would be at risk if a data center was built near the river. Meanwhile, some others at the meeting said the area needs more industry. Griffon Wilde, who owns property in Ellenburg Center, said she is skeptical of the project, but she’s also sympathetic to the local economy. "There needs to be new industry coming here. There needs to be more opportunities for people to be something other than prison guards," said Wilde. "There’s got to be more coming in for this place to survive.” "It sounds like there's still time for Chateaugay to potentially stop something like this," added Wilde, "or at least make sure that it will be a positive and bring enough jobs to make it worth it." Drafting up a moratorium At its meeting last week, the Chateaugay town board heard about 30 minutes of public comment on the potential data center. In the end, the board agreed to work on a one-year moratorium that would ban any data centers from coming to town. There is currently a statewide moratorium in effect, but it only applies to projects larger than 50 megawatts, so it would not apply to the proposed project in Chateaugay. After a local moratorium expires, town supervisor Don Bilow said if a data center is officially proposed in the future, he’d treat it like any other development. "Any project, we always look at it and go from there. If it looks like it’s going to benefit the community, we definitely move forward

artigo.texto: FLORIDA – The race for Florida governor is drawing sharp contrasts on some of the state’s most pressing issues. Democratic candidate David Jolly and Republican Rep. Byron Donalds sat down separately this week to answer questions on artificial intelligence, hyperscale data centers and Amendment 3, a property tax relief measure heading to voters next month. Here is where each candidate stands: Recommended Videos AI Data Centers Jolly said he would issue a moratorium on hyperscale data centers on his first day in office, arguing the industry is rushing into a state with a favorable regulatory and campaign finance environment before the public health and environmental questions have been answered. “This is moving too quickly,” Jolly said. “Big tech and big data are rushing into a relatively unregulated or favorably regulated environment.” Jolly pointed to a data center community in Northern Virginia where, he said, four children had been treated for respiratory conditions, one had been hospitalized, and several had been treated for hearing conditions. He said nearly 75% of Florida voters oppose the facilities. “Florida’s voters are saying, don’t do this. And I’ve said, I’ll issue a moratorium on my very first day in office,” Jolly said. Donalds took a different approach, saying the decision belongs to local governments — not the state. “County commissioners issue building permits, not governors,” Donalds said. “Local communities do.” Donalds said state law, signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis, already puts siting decisions in the hands of local communities. At the state level, he said his administration would focus on two guarantees: utility bills would not increase because of data centers, and fresh water would be protected through existing water use permit requirements administered by water management districts. Donalds also noted a study commissioned by the state is due back June 1, 2027, and said he would release it publicly. “We are going to maintain that,” Donalds said of the existing permitting framework. “This is not a new phenomenon.” Artificial Intelligence Jolly called himself an AI optimist but said the technology’s integration — not its promise — is the critical issue. He cited concerns about job displacement, children’s privacy and the role of AI in classrooms, arguing teachers should use AI as a tool, not be replaced by it. “AI should not replace a teacher,” Jolly said. “But I think teachers could benefit from AI.” He also cited what he described as a corrupt campaign finance system quieting public concerns. “The public is saying, hey, pump the brakes, slow down. Even the inventors of AI at times are saying, slow it down,” Jolly said. On job displacement, Jolly drew a comparison to trade adjustment assistance programs created during NAFTA and CAFTA, saying Florida may need a similar retraining and assistance framework if the federal government fails to act. Donalds said AI is already embedded in everyday life and cannot be put back in a box. “If you got rid of the models at the top four or five companies, there’s probably 500 young computer scientists and engineers who are already making up their own model,” Donalds said. He said Florida should focus on protecting children, safeguarding name, image and likeness rights, and empowering parents. He also pointed to commercial space development on the Space Coast as an example of AI-powered economic opportunity, calling it a potential $1 trillion industry generating high-paying jobs across multiple fields. “The question is, how do we protect families? How do we protect communities and how do we protect children?” Donalds said. Amendment 3 Both candidates acknowledged the property tax burden on Florida residents, but they land on opposite sides of the measure. Jolly said he anticipates voting no on Amendment 3, aligning with sheriffs and law enforcement groups who have warned the measure would cut funding for public safety services. “That’s essentially what Amendment 3 is gonna do. It’s gonna defund law enforcement along with critical services that communities need,” Jolly said. He said the measure was rushed through without a sufficient funding backstop and noted that Gov. DeSantis, who initially proposed a version of the idea, is not actively campaigning for it. Jolly said he would instead pursue targeted relief — a homestead exemption of up to $250,000 for first-time homebuyers, income-based relief for seniors, and returning expanded exemption authority to local governments. “Let’s target first-time homebuying tax relief,” Jolly said, noting the average age of a first-time homebuyer in Florida has risen from 28 to roughly 40 or 41 years old. Donalds said he supports Amendment 3, arguing property taxes on Florida residents have effectively doubled over the past seven years. “It’s not our money. It belongs to the citizen. It belongs to the taxpayer,” Donalds said. He said the amendment’s language requires public safety to be funded first before any cuts take effect. For fiscally constrained counties, he proposed a dedicated funding formula so those governments would not need to lobby Tallahassee for help. He also argued larger counties had the option to roll back tax rates as property values rose over the past six years and chose not to. “Local governments have to live within their means, the same way the state government has to live within our means,” Donalds said.

artigo.texto: Kandi secures CATL order: Kandi Technologies Group stock is valued at USD 68.6 million Published on 10/05/2026 at 01:02 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Kandi Technologies Group, Inc. (ISIN VGG5214E1034) secured a follow-on order for CATL heavy-truck battery-swap stations on September 28, 2026, as Kandi Technologies Group stock carried a USD 68.6 million market capitalization on October 2, 2026. The order marked the second batch tied to the company partnership with CATL within two months, according to Kandi Technologies. Battery swapping adds a second engine Kandi's China Battery Exchange subsidiary is building a battery-swapping equipment business alongside its electric off-road vehicle operations. The September 28 order gives that newer activity another commercial deployment milestone, while the company continues to sell utility vehicles, neighborhood electric vehicles, golf carts and off-road products. The CATL relationship matters because the follow-on order connects Kandi to heavy-truck infrastructure rather than only consumer and recreational mobility. The September 28 announcement therefore broadens the operating narrative from vehicle manufacturing toward equipment supplied for commercial transport. First-half revenue rose 57.4 percent For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Kandi reported USD 57.1 million of net revenue, up 57.4 percent from USD 36.3 million in the comparable period of 2025, according to StockTitan. Revenue from off-road vehicles and related parts increased 59.4 percent to USD 54.2 million, making that business the main quantified driver in the interim report. Gross profit rose 51.5 percent to USD 24.8 million in the first half of 2026, while gross margin eased to 43.5 percent from 45.2 percent. The combination shows faster sales growth alongside a modest contraction in gross profitability. Operating income turned positive Kandi reported USD 5.5 million of operating income for the first half of 2026, compared with a USD 1.9 million operating loss in the same period of 2025. Net income increased 452.2 percent to USD 9.4 million from USD 1.7 million, and diluted earnings per share reached USD 0.10 versus USD 0.02. The figures put operating execution beside the CATL order as the central issue for the company. Cash, restricted cash and certificates of deposit totaled USD 285.7 million as of June 30, 2026, while total assets stood at USD 461.4 million. Market value remains compact Kandi's market capitalization was USD 68.6 million as of October 2, 2026. The company is listed on Nasdaq under KNDI and operates in the consumer cyclical sector, with the industry classification Auto - Manufacturers. artigo.texto: SPOKANE, Wash. — The "Aquifers over AI" rally in Spokane on Sunday called for a statewide pause on new data centers, as organizers raised concerns about the impacts on water use and strain on local infrastructure. The event on Sunday was part of the Statewide Day of Action, where activists from across the state hosted rallies in many cities, demanding a statewide moratorium on new data center construction. Organizers said the push centered on protecting groundwater resources because they believed growing AI infrastructure could affect the city's aquifer. About 100 people attended the rally. Guest speakers from environmental nonprofit organizations also took part. The group started at the Riverfront Park Rotary Fountain, marched past City Hall and the Public Works building, and crossed the Monroe Street Bridge. Organizers said they wanted more transparency about the strain data centers place on regional infrastructure, noise pollution, and calls for more local and statewide moratoriums on new data centers. One of the organizers said the effort needed to go beyond Spokane and involve other communities. "Like, sure, it's great to pass in the city, but they're not going to build one here. It's going to be in the county. It's going to be in another city. Like this is why it's important that we build a coalition. We work with other jurisdictions; we work statewide to pass this moratorium," said Zenthia Peterson. Organizers also said the Spokane River was running the driest it had ever been and argued new data centers could make that worse. They said they hoped the turnout would send a message in support of a statewide moratorium against new data centers.

O mercado global de argamassas à base de cimento entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035. Esse crescimento é sustentado pelo aumento dos investimentos em infraestrutura de fabricação de eletrônicos, incluindo fábricas de semicondutores, data centers e instalações de montagem de precisão, onde as argamassas à base de cimento são essenciais para amortecimento de vibrações, estabilidade térmica e alinhamento preciso de equipamentos. As argamassas de alto desempenho, formuladas com modificadores poliméricos e aditivos especiais, representam 25–35% do valor do mercado global e avançam 6–8% ao ano, superando as formulações padrão. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, dinâmica da cadeia de suprimentos e posicionamento competitivo até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de argamassas à base de cimento prevê crescimento constante entre 2026 e 2035, com o consumo global avançando a uma taxa composta anual de 4–6%. Essa trajetória pressupõe a continuidade dos investimentos de capital em fabricação de semicondutores, data centers e automação industrial, além das atividades de manutenção e modernização de infraestrutura. As argamassas de grau padrão, usadas na construção geral e na alvenaria, crescerão 3–4% ao ano, enquanto as formulações de alto desempenho para aplicações de precisão avançarão 6–8%, ampliando sua participação no valor total do mercado. A Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo a região dominante, sustentada pelos polos de fabricação de eletrônicos na China, em Taiwan, na Coreia do Sul e no Sudeste Asiático. A América Latina e o Oriente Médio e África apresentarão maior dependência de importações, com a demanda atrelada a projetos de construção e energia de grande porte. artigo.texto: Volkswagen Rewires Battery Supply and Model Lineup as Margins Hit a Wall Published on 10/04/2026 at 19:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de Volkswagen is pressing ahead with a sweeping overhaul of how it builds cars and where it sources their batteries, even as the financial picture darkens. The Wolfsburg group has locked in a trio of battery joint ventures, signaled the arrival of an electric Tiguan, and opened a new round of labor talks — all while its shares scrape the bottom of a 52-week range. Three joint ventures, one trimmed stake Under an agreement dated September 28, Volkswagen Group, its in-house battery unit PowerCo SE and China's Gotion High-tech will establish three separate joint companies. The ventures will turn out LFP battery cells and cathode material at plants in Valencia, Spain; Šurany, Slovakia; and Kenitra, Morocco. The partners also plan to pool procurement and sales efforts across Europe. As part of the same arrangement, Volkswagen signed a binding deal to offload 5.3 percent of its holding in Gotion. The group will keep a meaningful stake once the transaction closes. Paris as a stage The battery pacts sit alongside a broader push to shore up its European base. On Thursday, ahead of an industry gathering in France, Volkswagen unveiled its "For Europe" initiative, pledging to strengthen European supply chains and safeguard future-proof jobs. Investment will concentrate on electric mobility, battery technology, software and artificial intelligence. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Volkswagen? A political and media exchange is set for Paris on October 11, followed the next day by the Paris Motor Show, where the Volkswagen, Audi, Škoda, CUPRA and Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles brands will roll out new models. Back home, the company confirmed the October debut of the ID. Tiguan, with the model's actual market launch slated for early 2027. Contracts on the table Labor relations form the other front. On Wednesday, management gave notice on several collective agreements effective December 31, 2026, while explicitly exempting the future collective agreement that guarantees job security. Revision talks have already begun, with further sessions with IG Metall scheduled for the second half of October. A warning that reset expectations These moves are unfolding against a sharply weaker backdrop. In mid-September, Volkswagen cut its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue of roughly EUR 315 billion and an operating margin of up to 1 percent. The company had previously targeted a margin of 4.0 to 5.5 percent. Management blamed restructuring costs, a tough market in China and a non-cash write-down of about EUR 6 billion on Porsche. Sentiment took a further hit roughly a week ago when Germany's KBA federal transport authority ordered a recall over a potentially corrosion-prone steering screw. Volkswagen at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Analysts trim their targets The revisions have rippled through brokerages. On September 21, Kepler Cheuvreux's Michael Raab downgraded the stock from "Buy" to "Hold" and cut his price target to EUR 80 from EUR 92, citing the reduced valuation headroom after the profit warning. That same day, DZ Bank's Michael Punzet lowered his fair value to EUR 73 from EUR 75, keeping a "Hold" rating and pointing to the reduced margin forecast for the year and more demanding targets through the end of the decade. A stock near its floor The market has taken notice. The shares are down 35 percent since the start of the year, and on Friday they closed at EUR 67.60 — barely above the fresh 52-week low of EUR 67.22 touched during the session. Investors will get a fuller read on October 29, when Volkswagen publishes its interim report for the first nine months. artigo.texto: BYD Files Immersion-Cooling Patent as JPMorgan Cuts Rating and September Volumes Roll In Published on 10/06/2026 at 12:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has lodged a patent application for a battery-cooling concept that submerges cell modules entirely in a dielectric fluid, adding a fresh layer to the Chinese automaker's technology pipeline even as its shares labour under a double-digit year-to-date decline. China's intellectual property authority published the filing yesterday, according to media reports. The original submission dates back to March 2025. Rather than routing coolant through channels along the outer faces of the modules, the described method lets a non-conductive liquid circulate directly around individual storage cells — an approach known as immersion cooling. That direct contact yields more uniform heat dissipation and can smooth out temperature spikes during operation. Thermal behaviour ranks as a decisive factor for the efficiency, durability and safety of high-voltage batteries, particularly under heavy charging loads or demanding use. September Output and Deliveries in Focus On the operational front, BYD reported production of 463,864 new-energy vehicles for September alongside sales of 463,561 units, figures the company flagged as preliminary and unaudited. Battery-electric passenger cars accounted for the bulk of deliveries at 273,143 units, while plug-in hybrids contributed 183,570 vehicles. Exports of new-energy vehicles reached 180,700 units during the month, underscoring the growing weight of overseas business. The broader picture is less buoyant. Across the first nine months of the calendar year, cumulative sales totalled 3,131,576 vehicles — a decline of 3.94 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. In German trading, the stock closed Monday at EUR 8.53, a daily gain of 1.6 percent. Since the start of the year, however, the shares have shed 20 percent. At a current price of EUR 8.52, the paper sits 6.1 percent above its 52-week low. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Model Offensive Meets a Regulatory Hurdle BYD is pressing ahead with an expansion of its line-up to reignite demand. Deliveries of the Formula S for the Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand began in late September, priced in China between 189,900 and 229,900 yuan. Management expects monthly sales of more than 10,000 to as many as 15,000 units over the medium term when the GT variant is included. Customer registration has also opened for the Ti 9, with first deliveries of the SUV flagship slated for the fourth quarter. A symbolic milestone arrived on the production line: on 29 September, the Da Han flagship sedan became the ten-millionth vehicle to roll off the Dynasty series. The official market launch of the new model is set for 13 October. Not everything went smoothly. China's market regulator announced a recall on 18 September covering 183,211 vehicles from the Tang and Qin model lines, citing potentially defective brake-pedal bump stops that the manufacturer will replace free of charge. JPMorgan Steps to the Sidelines Analysts at JPMorgan downgraded the stock from Overweight to Neutral on 29 September, trimming the price target to HKD 88 from HKD 124. The brokerage pointed to anticipated weakness in China's auto sector in the second half of 2026, subdued domestic demand and rising input costs. It also flagged political uncertainties and tariff as well as non-tariff trade barriers facing BYD's global expansion. Shareholders, meanwhile, signed off on governance matters at the most recent annual general meeting, approving charter amendments, board elections, director remuneration and an asset-pool transaction involving external guarantees. With the share price trading below its long-term moving averages, the market is showing restraint about the company's continued expansion and margin trajectory at home. artigo.texto: Pointo bets on e-auto, BESS, second-life battery segments to drive growth Lithium-ion battery startup Pointo plans to raise ₹70-100 crore to build an automated refurbishment unit and expand its distribution network Press Trust of India Kolkata WebinarsNew Deep DiveNew Explore Business Standard Lithium-ion battery distribution and service network startup Pointo is betting big on the expanding e-auto segment, battery storage systems (BESS) and second-life products to bolster its revenue, while actively engaging with investors to raise Rs 70-100 crore for its next expansion phase, a top company official said. The city-based startup, which previously raised Rs 6.2 crore in a seed funding round led by Equirus InnovateX Fund, plans to deploy the fresh capital to build an automated, large-scale refurbishment unit and expand its ground distribution network across the country. The company has seen its revenue run rate jump to Rs 80 crore in FY26 from about Rs 3 crore in FY24, and expects to close the current financial year at a revenue of Rs 150 crore, Founder & CEO of Pointo Riki Biswas told PTI. Founded in 2023 by Biswas, a chemical engineer from IIT Guwahati, along with three co-founders, Pointo aims to build a closed-loop supply chain across battery deployment, buyback, refurbishment and second-life applications. By eliminating high upfront costs and enabling instant access through financing tie-ups with non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), the company aims to redefine how India powers its electric vehicles (EVs). Biswas said the company has tied up with lithium-ion battery original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) for co-branding and marketing, alongside multiple NBFC partnerships to provide finance-ready lithium-ion batteries to e-rickshaw drivers and fleets. The startup currently serves 25,000 customers through more than 22 physical hubs spread across six states: West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Punjab. It is now looking to strengthen its micro-distribution network to reach Tier II and Tier III towns. "We are building a strong distribution network through a hub and spoke model, building a closed-loop supply chain across battery deployment, buyback, refurbishment and second-life applications. We are currently working in the e-rickshaw segment, which itself is a large market estimated at around 50 lakh vehicles. We will ramp up our presence in this segment," Biswas told PTI. "We also see a huge opportunity in the L5 E-auto, BESS and second-life products. We already have an existing distribution network, and we are looking to expand our network in the existing markets. This will enable us to tap into this growing demand efficiently," he added. Highlighting the market potential in the e-auto and four-wheeler segment, Biswas noted that starting next year, close to 8,000 to 10,000 electric autos are expected to come up for battery replacement, generating substantial demand for new lithium-ion batteries. The batteries retrieved during replacement will also serve as a key raw material source for second-life applications and new battery minerals. Pointo plans to convert end-of-life batteries into lower-use products such as home inverters for resale, helping shore up revenues while playing a crucial role in the circular supply chain. "We have a 20,000 sq ft R&D and refurbishment centre, and with a ready customer base, our next phase is to build an automated, large-scale refurbishment unit. We are in active discussion with investors to raise close to Rs 70-100 crore to build the refurbishment unit and expand the ground network," Biswas said. artigo.texto: Inlyte Energy, a United States-based iron-sodium battery storage manufacturer, has announced a long-duration storage project with CutPeak Energy at Berkshire East Mountain Resort in Massachusetts. The project has been designed around the resort's energy profile, since its snowmaking pushes the electricity demand as high as 4 MW for a small part of the year. An iron-sodium battery of up to 80 MWh is therefore to be recharged during the long hours of low demand and to deliver power through the snowmaking peaks. During a grid outage, the same battery can be switched to the critical loads which keep the resort open as a shelter and a warming centre. The project is one of two demonstrations that the state has selected under its $40.3 million Advancing Massachusetts Power Energy Storage Grant Program. Under that award, the battery is to come online in 2028, and the project remains subject to final agreements, financing and approvals. artigo.texto: Brasscom defende regulamentação imediata do Redata sem a parte das fontes de energia de baixa emissão "Essa parte das fontes de energia de baixa emissão está travando a regulamentação. Nós sugerimos fazer a regulamentação com todos os outros pontos acertados e fazer uma sobre essa questão depois. Precisamos acelerar. Quem perde é o Brasil", diz o presidente da entidade, Affonso Nina. A regulamentação do Redata está travada por conta da inserção do tema fontes de energia de baixa emissão no Senado, adianta o presidente da Brasscom, Affonso Nina, que participou da Futurecom 2026. O executivo disse à CDTV, do portal Convergência Digital, que apresentou a proposta de a regulamentação sair o quanto antes sem esse ponto das fontes de energia de baixa emissão. “Temos que acelerar e queremos a regulamentação o quanto antes. Nós fizemos a proposta de adiantar tudo que já está acertado”, afirmou Affonso Nina. O executivo admitiu que há dúvidas técnicas com relação à reforma tributária, mas disse que o Redata permite uma legislação ainda não existente no Brasil para o meio ambiente. Indagado se poderia haver algum data center já beneficiado pelo Redata ainda este ano, o presidente da Brasscom foi cauteloso e disse que tudo depende de quando a regulamentação vai sair e o quão rápido será a habilitação das empresas no benefício tributário. Sobre ICMS, Affonso Nina foi taxativo: O Redata sozinho não resolve uma vez que o ICMS responde por dois terços da carga tributária dos equipamentos. “Entendo os estados só quererem discutir uma possível redução de ICMS depois da regulamentação”, adiciona. Segundo ainda o presidente da Brasscom, a ‘bola agora’ está com o Poder Executivo. Assista a íntegra da entrevista.

artigo.texto: Mumbai: The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking is set to roll out a new generation of Olectra Greentech electric buses in Mumbai. The buses are equipped with advanced Blade Battery technology, which is expected to offer a longer range and enhanced safety. The first batch of 25 buses is expected to become operational by the end of the month, The Times of India reported. The buses are equipped with lightweight batteries that will enable them to operate for up to two days on a single charge. Batteries designed to conserve energy The batteries use lithium iron phosphate technology and are integrated into the bus chassis. They are reported to be capable of storing at least 30 percent more energy compared with batteries installed in existing air-conditioned buses. The new buses are also designed to offer improved safety and a longer range while operating at lower costs. Olectra supplying buses to BEST Olectra Greentech Limited is supplying the Blade Battery-based electric buses to BEST as part of efforts to meet Mumbai's public transport requirements. Technology designed for enhanced safety A senior Olectra Greentech official was quoted as saying by The Times of India: “Blade battery is designed to withstand extreme climatic conditions and is much safer even when severely damaged during accidents. It has very slow heat generation and no oxygen release. It is also more compact, increasing space utilisation in the battery pack by over 50%." Buses equipped with the similar battery technology are also operating in other cities across the globe, including London and Singapore, according to the report. artigo.texto: Kenya is set to receive KSh590 million in European Union climate funding to strengthen the systems used to monitor, report and verify carbon-market activities and national climate action, as the country moves to establish a more structured framework for participating in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The announcement was made in Nairobi on 5 October 2026 during the launch of the Kenya Guide for Strategic Engagement in Carbon Markets 2026, placing market integrity and institutional capacity at the centre of Kenya’s next phase of carbon-market development. EU Deputy Ambassador to Kenya Ondřej Šimíček said the funding, equivalent to about €4 million, would support Kenya’s monitoring, reporting and validation systems for both mitigation activities and national climate commitments. The support comes as Kenya seeks to create greater certainty for investors and project developers while ensuring that international transfers of carbon-related mitigation outcomes do not undermine the country’s own emissions-reduction commitments. The new Guide provides the institutional bridge between Kenya’s existing carbon-market regulations and the practical decisions required when projects seek to participate in international markets. Developed by the Government of Kenya with technical support from the Global Green Growth Institute’s Carbon Transaction Facility, it establishes principles, assessment criteria and implementation arrangements for evaluating and authorising carbon-market activities. It is intended to complement the Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024, which provide Kenya’s underlying legal and institutional framework for carbon projects. One of the most significant elements of the framework is its approach to the volume of mitigation outcomes Kenya can authorise for international transfer. The Guide establishes a national carbon budget for trading, effectively placing a ceiling on the quantity of mitigation outcomes that can be transferred internationally while protecting the country’s ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution. Independent analysis of the July 2026 Guide puts the cumulative ceiling at approximately 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent through 2030. That limit is important because Article 6 transactions involve more than the sale of conventional carbon credits. Article 6.2 provides rules for countries cooperating through internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, or ITMOs, while requiring accounting arrangements designed to prevent double counting. Article 6.4 establishes a United Nations-supervised mechanism for generating and trading carbon credits, while Article 6.8 covers non-market approaches to international cooperation. For Kenya, this means the government must be able to determine which mitigation outcomes can be transferred abroad, record those transfers and account for them against its national climate commitments. The country’s 2024 carbon-market regulations already provide for authorisation of ITMO transfers and require corresponding adjustments where applicable. They also require transferred mitigation outcomes to be recorded in the National Carbon Registry. The development of the registry has consequently become an important component of Kenya’s carbon-market architecture. The Kenya National Carbon Registry was formally launched in February 2026 and is designed to track, verify and manage carbon credits and internationally transferred mitigation outcomes. The registry is managed by the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA), which also serves as Kenya’s Designated National Authority for Article 6 and other carbon markets. The registry is intended to address one of the fundamental risks facing carbon markets: whether emissions reductions or removals can be uniquely identified, tracked and accounted for throughout their lifecycle. NEMA has said the registry will support transparency, prevent double counting and double issuance, and provide a national platform for recording carbon-market projects, authorisations and mitigation outcomes. The Guide adds another layer of decision-making by establishing clearer criteria for projects seeking government approval. It introduces a structured process for engagement and prioritises activities that align with Kenya’s climate and development objectives. The framework also places greater emphasis on environmental and social safeguards, stakeholder engagement, benefit sharing and the broader value that carbon projects can create beyond the sale of credits. That shift has implications for the investment market. Carbon projects are increasingly being assessed not only according to the number of credits they can potentially generate, but also according to whether their emissions reductions are measurable, additional, traceable and compatible with national climate policy. Weak monitoring systems or uncertain ownership and accounting rules can increase transaction risks and make international buyers more cautious. For Kenya, strengthening monitoring, reporting and verification therefore has an economic dimension. Credible systems can reduce uncertainty for investors, improve the ability of buyers to assess projects and provide government with stronger oversight of mitigation activities taking place within its borders. The EU funding announced in Nairobi is intended to strengthen precisely these institutional capabilities. The development also builds on a longer Kenya-EU climate partnership. European support has been directed towards renewable energy, climate resilience, sustainable agriculture and climate-governance systems, while Kenya has been developing its own institutional capacity for carbon-market participation. The EU has also supported wider climate and green-growth initiatives that seek to mobilise private investment alongside public and development finance.
