artigo.texto: BYD's Xixian Battery Plant Hits Full Throttle as Washington Delays Connected-Vehicle Ban Published on 10/04/2026 at 13:51 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD's newest battery cell facility in Xixian, Shaanxi province, has reached full production, the company's Yicai-reported milestone arriving just as its shares came under pressure from a global bond-market selloff. The plant, built at a cost of 7 billion CNY, carries an annual capacity of 16 gigawatt-hours and ranks among the first sites manufacturing BYD's second-generation Blade battery. Bringing cell production in-house is central to the automaker's strategy of keeping manufacturing costs in check. That operational progress, announced Wednesday, stood in contrast to the stock's performance. BYD shares finished Friday at 8.39 EUR on European trading venues, down 2.4% on the day, as surging US Treasury yields triggered a broad retreat across Asian equity markets. Several Chinese electric-vehicle makers, Li Auto and XPeng among them, fell in sympathy, though Geely managed to buck the trend. JPMorgan Cuts Its Rating Market sentiment was further dented by JPMorgan, which downgraded BYD from Overweight to Neutral and slashed its price target to 88 HKD from 124 HKD. The brokerage pointed to lackluster domestic demand, rising input costs, and persistent trade-policy and regulatory uncertainty facing Chinese carmakers. The downgrade was reported Wednesday, with some accounts placing the move a day earlier. The cautious stance reflects a home market where consumers remain on the sidelines. According to Reuters, BYD continues to grapple with weak demand in China, where a bruising price war has made buyers hesitant. Investors in Hong Kong responded tepidly to the company's latest disclosures, with the local listing slipping after trading resumed Friday. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Exports Do the Heavy Lifting September delivery figures, released Thursday, laid bare the split between home and abroad. Total vehicle sales climbed 17% year over year to 463,561 units, but the expansion was powered overwhelmingly by overseas markets: exports of passenger cars and pickups outside China jumped 153.9% to 179,877 units. Those booming shipments are doing much of the work of offsetting the sluggish domestic picture. The overseas push, however, cuts both ways. It opens fresh sales channels while drawing Chinese manufacturers deeper into the crosshairs of foreign regulators and trade officials. A Reprieve in Washington On that front, the US Senate on Wednesday postponed deliberations on a bill that would permanently bar the import, production, and sale of connected vehicles and related hardware and software with Chinese links. The delay hands Chinese automakers, BYD included, a temporary breather from looming restrictions on access to the North American market. For the year to date, unaudited company figures show total sales of 3,131,576 vehicles across the first nine months, a decline of 3.94% compared with the same period a year earlier. After the recent losses, the stock trades 4.5% above its 52-week low. The picture for investors is one of a company pulled in two directions: an overseas expansion that is generating real momentum, set against trade-policy decisions in Washington and elsewhere that remain a significant wildcard for the business ahead. artigo.texto: Nvidia e Broadcom se isolam de impacto de crise de energia em data centers dos EUA, diz Morgan Stanley 5 Out (Reuters) - Nvidia e Broadcom estão relativamente protegidas contra o agravamento da crise de energia nas centrais de processamento de dados dos Estados Unidos, afirmou o Morgan Stanley em relatório nesta segunda-feira. Porém, qualquer atraso resultante nas implantações de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial pode afetar os fabricantes de chips de memória, componentes ópticos e outros processadores secundários. O banco estimou no mês passado que os desenvolvedores de data centers nos EUA enfrentarão um déficit líquido de energia de 34% até 2028, equivalente a 32 GW. O boom da IA gerou bilhões de dólares em investimentos em data centers, mas as enormes necessidades de computação e eletricidade da IA generativa estão cada vez mais esbarrando nos problemas de fornecimento de eletricidade nos EUA. Tanto Morgan Stanley quanto Goldman Sachs sinalizaram restrições crescentes à expansão dos data centers nos EUA; o GS espera um impacto limitado no curto prazo devido à resistência política, enquanto o MS vê desafios relacionados à mão de obra, energia e política. O Morgan Stanley afirmou que não vê os gargalos colocando em risco as previsões da Nvidia ou da Broadcom para 2027, citando a visibilidade dessas empresas quanto à alocação de chips, à expansão geográfica e à coordenação entre centros de dados, fornecedores de chips e a cadeia de abastecimento de energia. Se a capacidade de produção de chips não puder ser implantada, os clientes poderão adiar entregas ou cancelar pedidos, sendo que componentes de memória, óptica, gerenciamento de energia e analógicos são os mais expostos a problemas de fornecimento, afirmou o Morgan Stanley. artigo.texto: Discussão na Cúpula: Solera, BYD e CITS Traçam o Futuro da Indústria NEV da China AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 5 de outubro de 2026 SHENZHEN, China, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — A Solera Holdings, LLC. (“Solera”), uma líder global em gestão do ciclo de vida de veículos e soluções digitais de segurança no transporte, recentemente fez uma visita de alto nível à sede global da BYD. A Sra. Jing Liao, Diretora Administrativa da Solera e Presidente da Solera Foundation, liderou a delegação da Solera em discussões com o Sr. Lian Yubo, Diretor de Tecnologia e Cientista Chefe da BYD, Engenheiro Automotivo Chefe, Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute e Acadêmico da Chinese Academy of Engineering, juntamente com sua equipe de gestão. A Sra. Yang Ying, Vice-Presidente e Secretária Geral da China Intelligent Transportation Systems Association (CITS), e o Sr. Wang Junming, Vice-Presidente da CITS, também participaram da reunião. A relação entre a BYD e a Solera começou há anos e vem se fortalecendo desde então mercado a mercado, desafio a desafio passando a ser a parceria ampla e global que as duas empresas trazem para discussão hoje. Esse nível de profundidade e abrangência só é alcançado após anos de trabalho conjunto em diversos mercados em todo o mundo. Esta visita marca o próximo capítulo: um compromisso compartilhado com o avanço da segurança rodoviária e a construção da infraestrutura que irá apoiar a indústria NEV da China na sua expansão em todo o mundo. Os participantes realizaram discussões aprofundadas sobre a expansão global da indústria de novos veículos de energia (NEV) da China, o desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de serviços no exterior, a colaboração internacional da indústria e as oportunidades futuras de cooperação. O Sr. SooCheon Chung, Diretor Administrativo da Solera na Ásia, e o Sr. Jason Liu, Diretor de Vendas da Solera China, também participaram da reunião. Foto: A equipe de gestão da Solera visita a Sede Global da BYD e posa para uma foto em grupo com o Sr. Lian Yubo, Diretor de Tecnologia e Cientista Chefe da BYD, Engenheiro Automotivo Chefe, Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute e Acadêmico da Chinese Academy of Engineering, sua equipe e líderes da CITS. Durante a reunião, foram realizadas discussões profundas sobre as oportunidades e os desafios enfrentados pelos fabricantes chineses de veículos de nova energia (NEV) na sua expansão para os mercados internacionais. As discussões se concentraram nos principais elementos do desenvolvimento do ecossistema pós-venda no exterior, incluindo gerenciamento do ciclo de vida do veículo, desenvolvimento da rede de serviços pós-venda, aprimoramento da capacidade de reparo, serviços de seguros e sinistros, desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de dados, e conformidade regulatória nos mercados globais. Na reunião também foram discutidos pontos de vista sobre o desenvolvimento de redes globais de serviços de pós-venda e a capacitação de talentos técnicos, abrangendo como informações de reparo, programas de treinamento técnico e ferramentas digitais podem apoiar a melhoria contínua das capacidades de reparo e da eficiência operacional nos mercados internacionais. Os representantes da Solera, CITS e BYD realizaram discussões sobre a expansão global da indústria NEV da China e o desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de pós-venda no exterior. Com a aceleração da expansão global da indústria NEV da China torna-se cada vez mais importante a construção de um ecossistema de serviços internacionais que dê suporte a todo o ciclo de vida do veículo. Durante as discussões, a equipe da BYD compartilhou insights da sua experiência com o crescimento internacional da empresa, incluindo perspectivas sobre o desenvolvimento da rede de serviços no exterior, recursos operacionais localizados e colaboração mais ampla do ecossistema da indústria. Os participantes também compartilharam pontos de vista sobre tópicos como acesso a informações de reparo e manutenção nos mercados internacionais, requisitos de conformidade de dados, e desenvolvimento de peças e ecossistemas de serviços. O Sr. Zhong Yilin, Vice-Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute da BYD, comentou: “A expansão da indústria NEV da China em todo o mundo está tornando cada vez evidente a importância da construção de ecossistemas de serviços robustos. O fortalecimento adicional das redes de reparo e serviço no exterior, o desenvolvimento de talentos técnicos e o aprimoramento das capacidades de serviço adaptadas às necessidades do mercado local são prioridades vitais para as marcas automotivas chinesas que buscam o crescimento internacional.” A Sra. Yang Ying, Vice-Presidente e Secretária Geral da China Intelligent Transportation Systems Association (CITS), endossou essa visão e acrescentou: O apoio ao desenvolvimento internacional das empresas chinesas NEV continua a ser uma área de foco essencial para a CITS. artigo.texto: Colleton County settles lawsuit, creating exclusion zone for data centers in ACE Basin WALTERBORO, SC (WCIV) — Colleton County has reached a settlement with the Southern Environmental Law Center that will prohibit data center development across much of the ACE Basin, ending a legal challenge over a county ordinance that opened rural areas to large-scale data center projects. The agreement resolves a lawsuit filed in January by Colleton County residents Miles Crosby and Jennifer Singleton, who challenged county zoning changes that allowed data centers in rural portions of the county through a special-exception process. Under the settlement, Colleton County will establish a "Data Center Exclusion Area" as part of its Comprehensive Plan, identifying areas deemed unsuitable for data center development. "This historic settlement agreement sets the framework for legislative action that will ensure responsible conservation of natural resources while securing the economic future for citizens of Colleton County," Colleton County Council Chairman Scott Biering said in a statement. The agreement follows months of intense public debate surrounding a proposed Eagle Rock Partners data center campus south of Walterboro. The project, first unveiled in late 2025, called for an approximately 859-acre, 1,000-megawatt development near the headwaters of the Ashepoo River in the ACE Basin, prompting strong opposition from residents concerned about impacts to the environment, water resources and the region's rural character. READ MORE | Colleton County residents raise concerns over proposed data center, power plant projects According to the Southern Environmental Law Center, the exclusion area will cover most of the ACE Basin within Colleton County, including ecologically sensitive lands along the Ashepoo, Combahee and Edisto rivers. The exclusion area also includes the roughly 850-acre tract where the original Eagle Rock proposal was planned. "The original data center complex that was proposed would have surrounded my property on three sides and completely changed the area," Miles Crosby said in a statement released by SELC. "I'm thankful we could reach an outcome that not only prevents data centers from surrounding my home but also protects the majority of the ACE Basin in Colleton County from data center development." Jennifer Singleton, another plaintiff in the case, called the settlement a compromise that protects one of South Carolina's most significant natural resources. "It's been a long and winding road to get here, but I'm thrilled we were able to reach a compromise that establishes a 'Data Center Exclusion Area' in Colleton County," Singleton said. "The ACE Basin is a treasure we must all work together to care for." County Administrator Thomas Higgs said the settlement demonstrates that economic development and environmental protection can coexist as South Carolina continues to attract new investment. "We understand South Carolina currently faces many economic development issues. Data centers are a current national security topic and developers have their eyes on South Carolina," Higgs said. "In every economic development scenario, the challenge is to protect South Carolina itself, and moreover, its natural resources." The ACE Basin encompasses roughly 1.6 million acres across the Ashepoo, Combahee and Edisto river systems and has long been recognized as one of the nation's most significant conservation landscapes. More than 300,000 acres have been permanently protected since the formation of the ACE Basin Task Force in 1989, according to SELC. SELC South Carolina Director Chris DeScherer called the settlement "a significant victory for the ACE Basin" and said the organization looks forward to working with county leaders to ensure future data center projects are developed responsibly. County officials said they hope the agreement can serve as a model for other South Carolina communities seeking to balance economic growth with conservation.

artigo.texto: [ESPAÑOL ABAJO | PORTUGUÊS ABAIXO] Colombia’s new government will initiate proceedings to lift a 50% cap on carbon credit retirements against CO2 tax liabilities – handing a win to voluntary carbon market (VCM) sellers, and boosting the significance of compliance measures in response to trade pressures from the EU. Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development Fabio Arjona announced in Medellin that the new government of right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella would propose the change to Congress. Latin American and Caribbean countries enjoy relatively low trade exposure to the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which prices in the embedded carbon of goods entering the bloc. Still, Colombia ranks just behind Brazil as the most EU CBAM-exposed Latin American or Caribbean countries. Colombia’s COP 29,070.49 ($8.76) per tonne CO2 tax rate may alleviate some of the border carbon burden by creating an EU-recognised domestic carbon price that’s deductible from CBAM fees. In its current form, the European Commission’s draft implementing act would make the price paid for carbon credits retired under the tax eligible for deductions, too – enhancing the role of the VCM to address both domestic and international carbon pricing compliance. Arjona simultaneously announced the revocation of Ministerial Decree 0973 on the VCM, which established restrictions in line with former President Gustavo Petro’s criticisms of the market and was published in early August. EMISSIONS TRADING SYSTEMS Both Colombia and Brazil are working to implement emissions trading systems – called the ‘PNCTE’ in Colombia, and the ‘SBCE’ in Brazil. These schemes could also create EU-recognised carbon prices. In Brazil, carbon project co-developer Earthshot Labs Brazil has seen some foreign investors take a cautious approach due to uncertainty in the SBCE’s final design, Carbon Pulse reported last week. That does not mean that investment in the Brazilian VCM has halted, according to the co-developer’s director Rita Croce – rather, some investors are holding out for projects that could potentially generate Article 6 Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) in the future. Brazil’s increasingly crowded carbon asset ecosystem would include SBCE allowances, called CBEs; SBCE-eligible voluntary carbon credits, called CRVEs; voluntary credits bearing a Letter of Authorisation; and regular voluntary units. Purchasing either CBEs or CRVEs for use in the SBCE could potentially fall under the European Commission’s draft vision for a ‘carbon price effectively paid’ in a third country, for CBAM purposes. Meanwhile, Colombia’s Ministerial Decree 0969 from the now-departed Petro administration stated that up to 3.3% of PNCTE compliance units could be sourced from the VCM – a far lower percentage than what was initially pitched in a Sep. 2024 consultation document. The fate of the PNCTE under De La Espriella is unclear. J-REDD+ QUESTIONS Meanwhile, a Brazilian state and Argentine province grappled with thorny implementation questions for jurisdictional REDD+ (J-REDD+). A proposed road in the Amazon could result in up to 133,800 hectares of additional deforestation over 20 years – putting Brazilian state Acre’s J-REDD+ goals at risk, according to a report published by NGOs Amazon Conservation and SOS Amazonia. Acre’s J-REDD+ programme is registered under the ART standard’s TREES protocol. Researchers noted that the modelling is not meant to predict actual future losses, but that plans for new road developments placed Acre at “a critical juncture”. In Argentina, senators for the province of Misiones – itself promoting a large-scale, Verra-registered J-REDD+ programme – are mounting partial opposition to a national bill they helped draft. Senator Sonia Rojas Decut has taken issue with the bill’s definition of ‘project owner’ (Spanish: titular del proyecto). The definition would effectively require written consent from thousands of native forest owners to implement programmes at the provincial level, she argued. The bill would therefore “make it impossible for Argentine provinces to implement jurisdictional programmes”, she wrote. Argentine media has reported that while the bill disappeared from the agenda for last week’s Senate session, members of ruling party La Libertad Avanza have indicated that they will participate in ongoing negotiations with Misiones in hopes of bringing the bill to a future session. NEWS By Alejandra Padin-Dujon – [email protected] [ESPAÑOL] Cambio de postura colombiana sobre la compensación de emisiones podría abrir oportunidades comerciales con la UE El nuevo gobierno de Colombia iniciará los trámites para eliminar el límite del 50% a la cancelación de créditos de carbono para cubrir obligaciones del impuesto al CO2, una medida favorable para los vendedores del mercado voluntario de carbono (VCM), mientras las medidas de cumplimiento cobran mayor relevancia ante las presiones comerciales de la UE. El ministro de ambiente y desarrollo sostenible, Fabio Arjona, anunció en Medellín que el nuevo gobierno del presidente derechista Abelardo De La Espriella propondría el cambio al Congreso. artigo.texto: KALAMAZOO, MI (WKZO AM/FM) – It has been one of the least controversial issues the Kalamazoo city commission has had to deal with this year, but one of the most emotional. Opinions have been nearly unanimous that the city needs to brace itself, and thoroughly prepare for the day someone wants to build a data center, or any other potentially worrisome high-tech facility in town. They have scheduled a final public hearing and a vote this evening. Kalamazoo city commissioners are set to finalize a one year moratorium, to buy time to redraft zoning codes to make sure if a data center or large battery energy storage system is proposed, that it won’t become a problem for its neighbors or the community. Assistant City Planner Bobby Durkee says that one year clock begins with tonight’s approval. “The goal of the moratorium is to develop those zoning standards and appropriate land uses, and to study for a transparent public process. For staff in the community to research the topic, understand the topic and draft regulations because you cannot outright ban a use.” He says as recommended by the planning commission, staff will set up a working group to assist in the research. “You know I look at things like public utilities, private utilities, residents, neighborhoods, the industry itself.” Several commissioners implored him not to make it top-heavy with industry and utility experts and to make sure it represents community and environmental interests too. Commissioner Chris Praedel says it’s “so critically important that there are people sitting in those seats that are just everyday people, you know, that care a lot about this issue.” While communities have some flexibility in how it sets up its own zoning regulations, it’s still a process that is guided by state laws and technical requirements and must be detailed and specific if a community wants to avoid legal challenges, or leave gaps or loopholes. Data centers have become a major state and national issue this election year with national polls showing 65 to 70% of the public opposed to having a data center in their community and only 20% supporting. The numbers are even higher for Democratic and younger voters.

artigo.texto: COLDWATER, MI (WTVB) – Coldwater city officials are in the process of trying to make the community as unattractive as possible to potential developers of data centers. This comes after a joint session on August 19 involving Coldwater government boards. They heard a presentation that evening on data centers from Jean Hardy of Michigan State University whose research centers on the role of technology in rural economic and community development. City Planner Robert Hawley told the Coldwater Planning Commission on Monday night they and their consultants from McKenna and Associates are currently working on zoning ordinance amendments that would define data centers. Mayor Tom Kramer emphasized there was no desire among City Council members to bring a data center to Coldwater. But Kramer added that by law, they have to offer something to potential developers. A draft could be presented to the Planning Commission on November 16 with a public hearing possibly taking place in December. Hardy said in August that the backlash across the state from communities opposing data centers has now caused those companies to rethink the prospects of building new facilities in the state. In other business, the Planning Commission approved a new Master Plan and sent it on to the City Council for final approval. It was compiled after a year of community surveys, steering committee meetings, and focus groups. The Master Plan for Coldwater has not been updated since 2017. It outlines goals and infrastructure strategies to guide the future growth of Coldwater.

artigo.texto: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee

artigo.texto: UAE-based real assets investor and developer ROX Capital Group has launched the ROX Gulf Energy Storage Platform, targeting utility-scale and commercial energy storage projects in the UAE and Oman while exploring opportunities for regional assembly and manufacturing. The platform will evaluate a range of storage technologies, including vanadium redox flow, lithium iron phosphate and sodium-ion batteries, as well as long-duration solutions such as CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage, compressed-air energy storage and thermal storage. ROX plans to establish partnerships with selected technology providers based on their track record in deploying large-scale storage projects, long-duration storage expertise where applicable, financial and operational capacity, and ownership or control of core technology intellectual property. The company said it will prioritise providers with bankable systems, established manufacturing capabilities and the ability to offer long-term technical support, performance guarantees and warranties. The platform and its partners will pursue upcoming energy storage tenders and assess local assembly or manufacturing opportunities where commercially viable. “The Gulf is building some of the world’s largest solar projects. The next challenge is ensuring that clean power remains available after sunset and during periods of peak demand,” said Robin Antony, Founder of ROX Capital Group. “No single technology will meet every requirement. We are building a platform that matches the right technology to the needs of each project and, where viable, supports the development of local manufacturing capability.” “Lithium-ion batteries have transformed energy storage and will remain an important part of the solution,” Antony added. “However, the Gulf’s climate, load profile and energy-security priorities create a need for a broader portfolio of technologies. High summer temperatures can increase cooling requirements, while solar-heavy systems require storage over longer periods after dark. We see an important role for technologies including vanadium flow batteries, CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage and thermal storage alongside lithium-ion solutions.” -TradeArabia News Service

artigo.texto: By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Oct. 5: Headway Earth and Rezonance, led by international carbon-market expert Dr. Divaldo Rezende, have launched the Carbon Market Development Mission Nepal to help develop the country’s emerging carbon-market and climate-finance ecosystem. The initiative aims to build Nepal’s capacity to develop climate projects, strengthen carbon-market infrastructure and connect Nepali projects with international climate finance, investors and carbon buyers. Nepal has significant potential in areas including forests, agriculture, renewable energy, waste management, biochar and other climate solutions. The mission seeks to turn this potential into bankable climate projects, investment, employment and sustainable development opportunities for Nepali communities and businesses, said Pratik Karki, Founder and Managing Director of Headway Earth. The mission will initially focus on three areas—capacity development, project development, and climate finance and market access. Under capacity development, the initiative will seek to strengthen knowledge, skills and institutional capacity among government agencies, financial institutions, businesses, communities and other stakeholders on carbon markets, climate finance and international climate policy, Karki added. Similarly, it will identify, design and develop high-quality climate and carbon projects across the country, with an emphasis on projects capable of attracting investment and delivering measurable environmental, social and economic benefits. The mission will also seek to connect Nepali projects with international investors, climate funds, financial institutions, development partners and carbon buyers, creating pathways for Nepali climate projects to access global markets. A key objective of the initiative is to help establish the institutional and financial infrastructure needed for a functioning national carbon ecosystem. Highlighting the opportunities in Nepal, Dr. Rezende said Nepal has an opportunity to strengthen international confidence and position itself as an attractive destination for climate investment. “The world wants to come to Nepal. Nepal is committing to zero corruption, and this can create a new level of confidence among international investors and climate partners,” he said. Dr. Rezende brings extensive international experience in carbon markets, climate finance and sustainable development. He will work alongside Headway Earth to support Nepal’s integration into global climate-finance and carbon-market opportunities. As part of its long-term vision, Headway Earth and Rezonance plan to work towards developing a Carbon Fund and Carbon Bank for Nepal to mobilise domestic and international capital for credible climate projects, said Prakash Gyawali, Chief Executive Officer of Headway Earth. The initiative also aims to support the development and integration of a national carbon registry and carbon marketplace to improve transparency, traceability and market access for Nepali carbon and climate assets. Technology and transparent measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) of climate impacts will form an important foundation of the proposed ecosystem. According to CEO Gyawali, the initiative is not limited to generating carbon credits but aims to establish the wider ecosystem required to support the carbon market, including projects, technology, finance, capacity, a registry, a marketplace and access to international markets.

artigo.texto: As if Emporia’s data center debate needed any more controversy. With the general election essentially a month away, Emporians for Progress spokesman Casey Woods says the ordinance language behind the petitions hoping to ban data centers and battery energy storage systems don’t reference city Planning and Zoning regulations currently on the books. The petitions reference Article 15, but Planning and Zoning code uses Sections instead of Articles and only goes up to Section 12. Emporia Neighbors United founder Jay Vehige sees things differently, although he admits there was a “drafting error” before the petition was turned in. The original petition and ordinance were submitted July 14, according to City Manager Trey Cocking. It was certified by the Lyon County Clerk’s Office on July 21 and was passed by the Emporia City Commission on August 5. Cocking says Vehige tried to submit revised petitions August 7, but he tells KVOE News cities have no ability to alter what was originally submitted — meaning residents have to vote on the original package due to KSA 12-3013. This is the second clerical or drafting error in this petition process for Emporia Neighbors United. The original petitions submitted were invalidated because petition circulators didn’t verify they witnessed petitions being signed. Vehige has told KVOE News that issue was due to a paperwork error in attaching circulator forms to signature petition forms. Woods says Emporians for Progress sees this as one reason to oppose the ballot questions. Vehige counters Woods’ assertions, saying his guidance indicates the Article 15 reference would not invalidate both petitions in their entirety. Vehige also says he has spoken with City Attorney Christina Montgomery, who was out of the office last week and is currently unavailable for an interview. Cocking sent a statement to KVOE News. saying the Article 15 reference will be one issue to be addressed by the court for effect and “enforceability.” He also says the city is not speculating how this will be addressed in court with that process a distinct possibility. Woods sees potential lawsuits throughout the 10-year halt if the questions are approved. The city has asked for rulings on whether the petitions are legislative or administrative in nature. Administrative rulings would likely invalidate the petitions — and, if the petitions are approved but Kansas Senior Judge Glenn Braun rules the petitions are administrative after the Nov. 3 general election, the vote results would be invalidated as well. Vehige believes Judge Braun will side with Emporia Neighbors United. There is no date for when Judge Braun will rule on the nature of the 2 ballot questions. This continues a busy time for news when it comes to data centers locally. A lawsuit filed by Emporia City Commissioner Erren Harter against Recall Committee members Haley Bradford, Kathleen Lamb and Vehige — also including Lyon County Legal Counsel Molly Priest and County Clerk Amie Jones as defendants — ended Thursday with an “agreed upon order” that essentially says this version of a recall petition cannot move forward under any circumstances. Priest and the case paperwork say this does not stop future petitions seeking Harter’s recall cannot move forward. A grand jury determining whether Harter conducted misconduct in office will be empaneled Monday. Meanwhile, Amanda Mendoza, Kenneth Bruner, Ann Bruner and the separate Bruner trusts have filed a lawsuit against the city of Emporia, alleging the zoning part of the Digital Infrastructure overlay was not properly handled. The lawsuit, LY-2026-CV-124, says the Emporia Planning Commission did not have either the jurisdiction or the authorization to review applications for zoning classifications that did not exist when applications were filed — meaning, according to the lawsuit, the city’s decision to approve the overlay was unlawful and the subsequent rezoning of 11 tracts of land was unauthorized and without proper jurisdiction. On top of that, Vehige says Emporia Neighbors United will push to bring 2 more petitions to the ballot by early next year. One would change the form of city government from its current at-large City Commission structure to a 4-ward City Council system with one at-large position. The other would change the method of filling unexpired City Commission or City Council positions from appointment to public vote. In separate news related to the Emporia data center project, the Flint Hills Digital Campus website is no longer public-facing. The website went public in early June as the data center project was announced. Project spokesman Garrett Nordstrom says flinthillsdigitalcampus.com was meant to be an informational site before rezoning and was meant to “dispel misconceptions.” Nordstrom says the website still exists but is internal now and is being shared with potential end users. Nordstrom says no end user has been selected for the proposed data center in west Emporia. He also says it would be unusual for a public website to document a private development project. The data center ballot questions will be part of KVOE’s political interviews later this month ahead of the general election Nov. 3. Appearing at 10:06 am Oct. 20 will be Vehige and Edgar Esparza from Emporia Neighbors United, as well as Woods representing Emporians for Progress. Our remaining interview slate is as follows: *Tuesday: Candidate Profile with Kansas House 13th District challenger Democrat Mark Remmert. Incumbent Republican Duane Droge did not confirm interest in a forum-style interview *Thursday: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 60th District challenger Democrat Maddison Glover and incumbent Republican Mark Schreiber *Oct 13: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 76th District nominees Democrat David Claridge and Republican Russel Stukey Click here for the KVOE Voter Information Guide courtesy Community National Bank & Trust.

artigo.texto: Strategic partnership targets commercialization of sulfide-based solid-state batteries Companies to jointly develop solid electrolytes and cathode materials for all-solid-state batteries Ecopro BM announced Tuesday that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Samsung SDI to cooperate on developing materials for all-solid-state batteries, with the goal of commercializing sulfide-based solid-state batteries by 2027. The two companies plan to deepen cooperation across the entire development process — from early-stage research through quality evaluation and the establishment of mass production systems — to raise both technological maturity and business competitiveness. They also intend to expand the scope of collaboration to cover a broad range of key materials, including cathode materials for all-solid-state batteries, cathode electrolytes and separator electrolytes. Under the agreement, Samsung SDI will advance cell development and refine its mass production technology for all-solid-state batteries, while Ecopro BM will take charge of developing the key materials. All-solid-state batteries are widely regarded as a next-generation technology capable of improving safety and performance at the same time. Because they offer longer use per charge and reduce the risk of fire, they are considered a core technology for future industries such as electric vehicles and humanoid robots. Ecopro BM has developed proprietary process technology in sulfide-based solid electrolytes — a critical material for all-solid-state batteries — and operates a pilot plant with an annual production capacity of 40 tons. The company is strengthening its technological edge through powder-control and quality-management capabilities, which are central to solid electrolyte development. It is also developing cathode materials suited to solid electrolytes, drawing on its high-nickel cathode technology. In recognition of these research and development achievements, Ecopro BM was selected in August for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's "Super-Eul Project." The program is a government-backed research and development support initiative aimed at nurturing key materials, parts and equipment companies capable of leading global supply chains by securing world-class, first-of-their-kind technologies. Companies selected for the program submit their own growth strategies and technology development plans to the government, which then evaluates them through a review of the proposal, technical verification and a comprehensive assessment. Ecopro BM passed the government's evaluation with its sulfide-based solid electrolyte project. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy plans to provide selected companies with large-scale research and development support of 20 billion won ($14.7 million) per project over seven or more years. The ministry released a "Battery Industry Technology Roadmap" last month, designating all-solid-state batteries as a core strategic technology for the future battery industry. The government said it plans to support the early commercialization of next-generation batteries by strengthening joint research and development between cell and materials companies and deepening supply chain cooperation. Ecopro BM had earlier outlined a full value-chain roadmap for all-solid-state batteries at an investor relations event for retail investors in July. Gong Bo-hyeon, executive vice president for research and development at Ecopro BM, said at the time regarding solid electrolyte development: "We are currently reviewing trial production with leading customers, and we expect the earliest mass production timeline to be 2027. We have completed the design of the mass production line and are preparing to break ground immediately in line with customer demand." Meanwhile, Song Ho-jun, chief executive of Ecopro, was named incoming chief executive of Ecopro BM in a reshuffle of Ecopro Group's presidential-level executives last Wednesday. Under Song's leadership, Ecopro BM plans to strengthen its role as an intermediate holding company overseeing secondary battery materials. The company also intends to complete management systems at its overseas subsidiaries in Hungary and Canada, and to focus on building future growth engines through investment in the BNSI smelter in Indonesia. likehyo85@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: We sat down with Norfolk-based artist Rhashida Bess to talk about jewelry making and upcoming programs. Who is Rhashida Bess? Rhashida is the owner and operator of Alodeuri (pronounced al – oh – durr – ee) Artisan Jewelry, an African-inspired, cold form metal smithing and jewelry-making business. A skill she first learned in high school and advanced through self-teaching, jewelry making launched Rhashida into the world of entrepreneurship when she was looking for a way to turn her hobby into a way to provide for her family. Rhashida’s adornments (the term she uses for her handmade, sustainable, intention-based jewelry pieces) incorporate materials such as copper, brass, cowrie shells, semi-precious stones and crystals. How did she get started with NPL? Rhashida started working with NPL after attending a program. While talking with another library patron about her personal business, she was approached by a staff member who asked if she, with her wealth of experience, might be interested in teaching a program at the branch. What does Rhashida love about working with NPL? Rhashida loves teaching library patrons about the history of traditional jewelry and supporting them on their jewelry-making journey. Rhashida believes in teaching people both new skills and how to use those skills to achieve future financial stability. While Rhashida’s true love is copper-based jewelry, particularly chains, she dabbles in a variety of types and techniques, including beading and paper rolling. Some of the many programs Rhashida has done with NPL include Weaved Words Bangles, Maasai-inspired earrings and Crystal Point Necklaces. Upcoming Programs This fall, Rhashida will be holding The ARTisan Academy at Jordan-Newby Anchor Branch. Join her select Thursdays from 5:30 – 7:30 p.m. to invest 24 hours in yourself to change the rest of your life! This vocational pathway to creative entrepreneurship will teach you how to create adorned jewelry and birth a microbusiness. Fun Fact: Alodeuri is a blend of her children’s names. Fun Fact 2: Her favorite material to work with is copper.

artigo.texto: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have recently been drawing growing attention in the battery industry. While solid-state batteries, noted as the ‘dream battery’ for their high energy density, have attracted interest for future industries such as robots and high-performance electric vehicles (EVs), ‘price competitiveness’ is becoming crucial for applications such as energy storage systems (ESS) and mass-market EVs. Sodium is the English name for natrium, and SIBs are also called ‘salt batteries’. They charge and discharge by sodium ions, rather than lithium ions, moving between the cathode and anode. Because sodium, the key raw material, is abundant and sourced from a relatively wide range of regions, it can reduce raw-material price volatility and supply-chain risk. They are safe and maintain performance at low temperatures, raising expectations for broad application from ESS and EVs to automotive auxiliary power and uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) for data centers. This is why SIBs do not hide their ambitions to be an ‘all-weather battery’. Batteries, is ‘performance above all’ not everything? Humanoid robots and the like are emerging as new future sources of battery demand, but the largest markets remain EVs and ESS. Market researcher TrendForce estimates annual demand for solid-state batteries for humanoids at 74 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in 2035. By contrast, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA) and BloombergNEF, EV battery demand in the same year is projected at 4,0005,000 GWh, with new ESS installations reaching 972 GWh. The issue is that the importance of the ‘price factor’ is growing in both markets. In EVs, high-energy-density batteries are drawing attention for large, long-range, high-performance vehicles, while cost-competitive batteries are in focus for compact, urban models. ESS, where weight and volume constraints are relatively modest, is no different in the importance of price. The overall leveling-up of batteries is also heightening the importance of price. According to the IEA, the latest SIBs reach up to 175 watt-hours (Wh) per ㎏, falling short of the latest lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries (205Wh/㎏), but they have risen to the range of typical LFP levels (150~200Wh/㎏). China is moving to preempt the SIB market. After unveiling its SIB brand ‘Naxtra’ last year, CATL this year revealed a passenger car equipped with SIBs together with Changan Automobile. For ESS-use SIBs, it is targeting cumulative shipments of 1 GWh by year-end. According to the IEA, more than 95% of SIB production capacity in 2030, combining existing and planned facilities, is expected to be concentrated in China. Three Korean battery makers say, “This time is different from LFP”…gearing up to target SIB Korean battery makers are also accelerating development of batteries such as SIBs. This is because global SIB production capacity is still just over 1% of that of lithium-ion batteries, making it an early-stage market. A battery-industry source said, “There was a case in which domestic response to LFP was delayed in the past, so there is a mood not to fall behind in the early leadership race for the SIB market.” According to an announcement by SNE Research on the 2nd, global EV battery usage reached 844.2 GWh in JanuaryAugust this year, up 19.7% from the same period last year, but the combined share of the three Korean firms fell from 16.6% to 12.7%, down 3.9 percentage points. Meanwhile, the share of LFP batteries, where Chinese companies are strong, rose from 52.2% to 57.3%. SIBs are therefore also a future strategy to gain a competitive edge in the mass-market battery segment centered on China. LG Energy Solution is testing 12V (volt) and 24V packs for automotive auxiliary power on customer vehicles. It has completed technology validation in the hundreds of ㎿h(megawatt-hours) range with long-cycle ESS customers, and from next year plans to ship trial volumes to global customers. SK On plans to develop an ESS-use SIB prototype next year and commercialize it in 2028, and is also reviewing SIBs for EVs. Samsung SDI is developing SIBs for UPS and power ESS. The Korean government has set a goal of securing an SIB energy density of 160Wh/㎏ by 2027 and raising it to 220Wh/㎏ by 2030 for commercialization. ‘Will it catch LFP, or remain a niche?’…diverging views However, opinions diverge on whether SIBs will grow enough to threaten the position of LFP. Those who view SIBs as a future growth engine are pinning hopes on price declines with future mass production. Because supplies are nt concentrated in specific countries as with lithium, raw-material supply instability is lower, and aluminum can replace copper for the anode current collector, reducing costs. If pack structures are simplified by leveraging SIB safety, system-level costs can also be reduced. Conversely, as LFP is also raising energy density and compensating for weaknesses through design improvements, there is analysis that it is uncertain whether SIBs will fully replace LFP. Because each battery type has different strengthssuch as low-temperature performance, energy density, output, and safetySIBs should be seen as just ‘one option’ to broaden the battery portfolio. Can Korea catch up with China, which is in the lead? For Korean companies, the key question is whether they can secure competitiveness that surpasses China. In particular, in the early SIB market, how quickly they can narrow the mass-production gap with China and, at the same time, secure non-China material supply chains and customers will likely determine future competitiveness. In this respect, the United States push to build a de-China battery ecosystem is a positive factor. However, it is a burden in practical terms that China is already ahead in industrialization. artigo.texto: A recent study in PRX Quantum from the University of Oulu identifies key limits on quantum battery reliability and shows how different charging protocols can balance high power output with steady, predictable energy and power delivery. The findings help clarify what “dependable” performance will require in practice, bringing usable quantum energy-storage systems a step closer. Quantum uncertainty imposes a fundamental trade-off in quantum batteries, limiting their ability to deliver steady power and reliable energy simultaneously. Quantum batteries are an emerging area of research, with progress coming from theoretical work and early proof-of-concept experiments in small quantum systems. Unlike the chemical batteries used in everyday devices, quantum batteries store and transfer energy using quantum states. Researchers are exploring them as potential power sources for quantum processors and other quantum technologies. Much of the early work has focused on how quickly and efficiently these batteries can be charged. In their recent study, the team identified fundamental limits on fluctuations in both the energy a quantum battery delivers and the rate at which it supplies that energy. A quantum battery ideally should not only be fast and powerful but also needs to charge or deliver energy in a reliable and stable manner at the same time. Our work shows that quantum mechanics places fundamental limits on the reliabilities of quantum batteries. Brij Mohan, Study First Author and Postdoctoral Researcher, University of Oulu The researchers show that a familiar cornerstone of quantum mechanics, the uncertainty relation, prevents energy fluctuations and power variations from being minimized at the same time. In other words, a quantum battery cannot be tuned to deliver both highly reliable energy transfer and perfectly steady power at the same time. Here, “stability” and “reliability” mean keeping fluctuations small relative to their average values. The trade-off arises because, in closed quantum batteries, work and power are represented by non-commuting operators, much like position and momentum in standard quantum mechanics. The team then examined how this trade-off relates to methods for charging multiple quantum battery cells. In parallel charging, the cells function autonomously. Collective charging involves all cells simultaneously. Hybrid charging represents a midpoint between these two approaches, in which groups of cells interact during the charging process. The findings indicate that more robust collective charging increases power but also amplifies power fluctuations, which reduces power reliability. This suggests that evaluating quantum-battery performance based solely on maximum power is inadequate. Our results show that there is a meaningful way to balance power enhancement and the reliability of work and power. Intermediate-range interactions based charging scheme can provide a useful compromise between high power and stable operation. Tanmoy Pandit, Research Scientist, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland The researchers further investigated quantum batteries with transverse Ising-type many-body interactions and found a similar qualitative trade-off between power and reliability. This finding suggests that the phenomenon is not limited to the most basic theoretical framework. The reliability limits connect quantum fluctuations with many-body quantum physics in a direct way. They provide useful charging strategies that are practically advantageous. Manabendra Nath Bera, IISER Mohali “Quantum batteries offer a fascinating link between quantum information, thermodynamics, and many-body physics. Understanding their fluctuations is essential if these systems are eventually to become useful technological resources,” added Maciej Lewenstein, ICFO, Spain. The researchers' next goal is to explore the limits of reliability in more practical environments, accounting for factors such as noise, energy loss, open-system behavior, and experimentally relevant quantum platforms. Quantum batteries represent an ongoing advancement stemming from the extensive research conducted by the Nano and Molecular Systems Research Unit at the University of Oulu. This research focuses on the theoretical and modeling aspects of quantum devices, including superconducting qubits and quantum processors. Journal Reference: Mohan, B., et al. (2026) Fundamental Limitations on the Reliabilities of Power and Work in Quantum Batteries. PRX Quantum. DOI:10.1103/fnv6-yqmk. https://journals.aps.org/prxquantum/abstract/10.1103/fnv6-yqmk.

artigo.texto: EcoPro BM is strengthening its cooperation with Samsung SDI on materials development aimed at commercializing sulfide-based solid-state batteries. EcoPro BM said Oct. 6 that signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Samsung SDI to develop materials for solid-state batteries. The two companies will jointly develop battery cells and key materials, targeting commercialization in 2027. Their cooperation will span from early-stage research and development through quality evaluation and the establishment of mass-production systems. Samsung SDI will advance solid-state battery cell development and mass-production technology. EcoPro BM will develop key materials, including cathode materials for solid-state batteries, electrolytes for cathodes and electrolytes for separators. EcoPro BM operates a pilot plant with an annual capacity of 40 metric tons for producing sulfide-based solid electrolytes. The company is also developing cathode materials suited to solid-state batteries using its high-nickel cathode technology. EcoPro BM was selected in August for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's "Super Eul Project" for its sulfide-based solid-electrolyte technology. In July, the company identified 2027 as the earliest possible timing for mass production of solid-state battery materials.

artigo.texto: India is stepping up investment in battery energy storage systems (BESS) to stabilize its power grid. The government plans to invest 500 billion rupees to deploy 50 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of BESS by 2033. According to industry sources on Oct. 6, the Indian government approved the third phase of the Green Energy Corridor (GEC-III) on Sept. 30. The project will expand transmission networks and BESS in line with the country’s growing renewable energy capacity. India plans to build transmission infrastructure capable of accommodating up to 135 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy by 2033. It will also install 50 GWh of BESS. The total project cost is 1.864 trillion rupees. Of that amount, 500 billion rupees has been allocated for BESS deployment. The government has not disclosed detailed conditions for the batteries to be used in the project, including battery chemistry, storage duration and procurement methods. The actual amount spent on batteries and systems could vary depending on those conditions. On a simple calculation, India will need more than 7 GWh of batteries annually for grid-scale energy storage systems (ESS) alone. But local battery production capacity is only about 2 GWh a year, meaning the country will have to rely heavily on imports. India has largely met demand through imports as it was late to establish a lithium-ion battery manufacturing base. Chinese-made batteries accounted for 75.2% of India’s lithium-ion battery imports in fiscal 2024-25. According to the India Energy Storage Alliance (IESA), India’s lithium-ion battery production capacity could reach 60 GWh to 70 GWh by 2030 if announced investment plans are implemented as scheduled. Over the same period, capacity for assembling battery packs and BESS using imported cells is expected to rise to 180 GWh to 220 GWh. Local cell production is therefore expected to lag well behind the expansion of BESS manufacturing capacity. Wood Mackenzie estimates that it will take India 10 to 15 years to build a self-sufficient battery industry with competitive pricing. It estimates that locally produced battery cells will cost 25% to 40% more than imported cells. High financing costs and an underdeveloped battery-materials supply chain are among the reasons. As India needs time to expand domestic battery production, it will have to rely on overseas technology and supply chains for the time being. That could create an opportunity for Korean companies to enter the market. Indian companies have traditionally worked mainly with Chinese battery makers because of their price competitiveness. But the business environment is changing as political tensions between India and China persist. Korean companies are also seeking opportunities to enter the Indian market. AI battery startup DeltaX signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Toptec in July to cooperate on targeting India’s ESS market. “India is expanding localization across its renewable energy industry, including requiring the use of domestically produced solar panels,” DeltaX Chief Executive Kim Soo-hoon said. “Local solar and renewable energy companies are also expanding into assembling and selling battery modules and packs for ESS, and are actively considering cooperation with companies outside China.” The growing adoption of Korean-made battery equipment in India is another positive factor. A key example is a battery plant with annual capacity of 40 GWh being built in India by Agratas, a Tata Group company. A number of Korean battery-equipment makers, including Yunsung F&C, PNT, Philenergy, Hana Technology, J's Robotics and Axvis, have been selected as suppliers for the project. Business by Korean battery manufacturers in India remains limited. LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI operate local sales subsidiaries, but their main business is supplying small batteries for smartphones and other information-technology devices. Their operations in India remain small in both scope and scale compared with major overseas markets such as North America and Europe. LG Energy Solution leads among companies in energy-related patents, having filed 2,225 patents in India. “Indian ESS companies have traditionally sourced battery cells mainly from Chinese companies,” an industry official said. “They also prefer lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, so opportunities for Korean battery companies to enter the Indian market could expand as they increase their LFP-related businesses.” India also built a large-scale power grid under previous phases of the Green Energy Corridor program. Phase I involved about 9,100 kilometers of transmission lines, while Phase II is adding about 7,900 kilometers across seven states. As transmission investment expands under Phase III, demand is also expected to rise for power equipment from HD Hyundai Electric, LS ELECTRIC and Hyosung Heavy Industries, alongside BESS.

Targeting Commercialization by 2027 Joint Development of Sulfide-Based Solid Electrolytes and All-Solid-State Cathode Materials Expanding Collaboration from Cell Development to Core Materials and Mass Production Systems Ecopro BM is joining forces with Samsung SDI in developing core materials and building a supply chain, aiming for the commercialization of sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries next year. Ecopro BM announced on the 6th that it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Samsung SDI for cooperation in developing materials for all-solid-state batteries. The two companies plan to strengthen collaboration from the early stages of development through quality assessment and mass production system establishment, with the goal of enhancing the technological completeness and business competitiveness of all-solid-state batteries. Image of all-solid-state battery materials unveiled by Ecopro BM at InterBattery in March. Ecopro BM View original image Under the agreement, Samsung SDI will be responsible for developing all-solid-state battery cells and advancing mass production technology. Ecopro BM will be in charge of developing core materials for all-solid-state batteries. The two companies will expand the scope of their cooperation to include not just cathode materials for all-solid-state batteries, but also electrolytes for cathodes and electrolytes for separators. All-solid-state batteries are next-generation batteries that use a solid electrolyte instead of the conventional liquid electrolyte. They are considered key technologies for future industries such as electric vehicles and humanoid robots, as they can improve energy density and safety. Ecopro BM has secured proprietary processing technology in the field of sulfide-based solid electrolytes, a core material for all-solid-state batteries, and operates a pilot plant with an annual capacity of 40 tons. Leveraging its powder control and quality management technologies, the company is enhancing its competitiveness in solid electrolytes while also developing cathode materials optimized for solid electrolytes using its high-nickel cathode technology. Based on its sulfide-based solid electrolyte technology, Ecopro BM was also selected in August for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's "Super Eul Project." The Super Eul Project is an R&D support program designed to foster materials, parts, and equipment companies capable of leading global supply chains. The government plans to support each selected company with more than 20 billion won of long-term R&D funding per project over at least seven years. Last month, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy released the "Battery Industry Technology Roadmap," designating all-solid-state batteries as a key strategic technology for the future battery industry. The government plans to support the early commercialization of next-generation batteries by strengthening joint R&D and supply chain cooperation systems among cell and materials companies. artigo.texto: Novo regime tributário reduz custos para o setor e pode acelerar investimentos em data centers, enquanto a HostDime prepara em João Pessoa uma estrutura de R$ 250 milhões voltada a aplicações de inteligência artificial avançada O novo Redata pode provocar uma arrancada dos data centers no Brasil nos próximos anos. A avaliação é do CEO da Positivo Tecnologia, enquanto João Pessoa já aparece nesse movimento com um projeto de R$ 250 milhões voltado à inteligência artificial. Redata pode destravar uma fila de projetos no país A capacidade instalada de centros de processamento de dados no Brasil pode dobrar ou até triplicar nos próximos dois ou três anos. A projeção foi feita por Hélio Bruck Rotenberg, CEO da Positivo Tecnologia. Segundo o executivo, havia projetos aguardando uma definição sobre os incentivos tributários antes de avançar. Com o novo regime aprovado, a expectativa dele é de uma corrida por servidores, componentes e outros equipamentos necessários para colocar esses empreendimentos de pé. - Nova ponte de R$ 6,2 milhões vai sair do papel em Erechim e licitação já tem data marcada para começar - Multinacional alemã prepara investimento de R$ 712 milhões em Santa Catarina com construção de nova fábrica e expansão capaz de elevar produção em 130% - 40 mil pessoas a pé no meio dos caminhões: Via Dutra fecha 45 km de faixa com cones e leva à ANTT plano de calçada até Aparecida - De olho na indústria de rochas do ES, grupo italiano investe R$ 60 milhões para ampliar fábrica e elevar produção de 18 mil para 30 mil toneladas ao ano O Paraíba Business destacou que esse cenário já alcança o Nordeste e colocou a Paraíba no mapa dos novos investimentos, especialmente por causa da expansão da HostDime em João Pessoa. Rotenberg resumiu sua expectativa sobre o tamanho desse salto: “Acredito que deva duplicar ou triplicar nos próximos dois ou três anos”. A previsão é do executivo e, portanto, não representa uma projeção oficial do governo. Lei do Redata corta tributos e cria contrapartidas O Redata virou lei em 15 de setembro de 2026. A Lei nº 15.504 criou o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter e entrou em vigor na data de sua publicação. O programa prevê benefícios tributários para equipamentos e componentes destinados aos centros habilitados. Entre os tributos abrangidos estão Imposto de Importação, IPI e PIS/Cofins, incluindo cobranças incidentes sobre importações. Não é simplesmente uma liberação de imposto. Quem entrar no regime precisa cumprir contrapartidas, incluindo investimentos em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação e regras relacionadas ao atendimento do mercado brasileiro. De acordo com o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços, ao menos 10% da capacidade de processamento, armazenagem e tratamento deverá ser disponibilizada ao mercado nacional ou destinada, nas condições previstas, a instituições científicas, tecnológicas ou ao poder público. Para projetos localizados no Norte, Nordeste e Centro-Oeste, a própria legislação prevê redução de 20% em determinadas contrapartidas. Esse ponto ajuda a colocar regiões fora do eixo tradicional do Sudeste na disputa pelos novos empreendimentos. Antes da aprovação, entidades empresariais apontavam uma diferença pesada no bolso. Segundo manifesto do setor produtivo, instalar um data center no Brasil custava 26% mais que nos Estados Unidos e 35% mais que no Chile. Data center de R$ 250 milhões coloca João Pessoa nessa corrida Na Paraíba, o projeto mais concreto é da HostDime Brasil. A empresa anunciou investimento de R$ 250 milhões para ampliar sua infraestrutura de data center em João Pessoa. A estrutura terá capacidade energética de até 15 megawatts e será preparada para cargas de inteligência artificial. A própria companhia também cita tecnologias de refrigeração líquida para lidar com servidores de alta densidade. A HostDime já mantém operação na capital paraibana. A nova estrutura representa uma expansão bem maior e mira aplicações que exigem muito poder computacional, justamente o tipo de demanda que cresceu com modelos de inteligência artificial. Há, porém, uma diferença importante nas datas divulgadas. A reportagem do Paraíba Business publicada em 5 de outubro informa que o novo centro deverá operar em 2027. Já comunicações da própria HostDime publicadas em setembro colocam o início da operação em 2028. Também há variação sobre o começo das obras: um conteúdo da companhia, de 8 de setembro, mencionava início ainda em 2026; outro, publicado em 16 de setembro, indicava construção a partir de 2027. O investimento de R$ 250 milhões e a capacidade projetada de 15 MW permanecem nos materiais da empresa. Expansão no Brasil também mexe com fabricantes O movimento não interessa apenas a quem constrói os galpões cheios de servidores. Para fabricantes de equipamentos, uma expansão rápida dos data centers pode abrir um mercado grande dentro do país. A Positivo Tecnologia já atua na fabricação de servidores e vê no Redata uma oportunidade de ampliar essa frente. Rotenberg também defendeu que a política permite trazer tecnologias ainda não produzidas localmente sem retirar espaço da indústria já instalada no Brasil. A lei diferencia ainda a tributação de bens importados. O regime suspende impostos dentro das condições previstas e estabelece regras específicas para estimular investimentos, ao mesmo tempo em que exige aportes em pesquisa e desenvolvimento. O tamanho real dessa expansão, no entanto, ainda será medido nos próximos anos. Dobrar ou triplicar a capacidade é uma projeção do CEO da Positivo, não uma meta legal do Redata. Por enquanto, o que já está definido é o novo regime tributário. E, na Paraíba, há um investimento anunciado de R$ 250 milhões que coloca João Pessoa entre as cidades que tentam ganhar espaço na nova infraestrutura digital brasileira. Fonte: Paraibabusiness.

artigo.texto: São Paulo recebe, desde esta terça-feira e até esta quinta um dos maiores eventos globais de tecnologia voltada ao setor empresarial. O Data Center World Brasil, realizado no São Paulo Expo, é focado em soluções para companhias em áreas estratégicas, algumas das quais o Rio Grande do Sul tem sido um player cada vez mais competitivo, como a instalação de data centers, com oportunidades em negócios nas áreas de hardware, equipamentos e investimentos em geral. Prestes a completar 30 anos no Brasil, a Kingston, mais conhecida no mercado consumidor tradicional como fabricante de memórias e pendrives domésticos, busca acelerar sua atuação na infraestrutura corporativa no mercado latino-americano com outros produtos complementares, inclusive voltadas a relacionamentos, como parcerias com marketplaces. O Brasil, atualmente, concentra 58% da fatia de mercado da Kingston na América Latina e somente as vendas da linha enterprise cresceram 42% no primeiro semestre deste ano. “O Brasil hoje é o principal polo de data center na América Latina. A gente tem muita energia limpa no país e já possuímos vários cabos submarinos. Hoje um dos principais gargalos de construir data center no mundo é a questão da energia, e isso o Brasil tem bastante”, destacou o country manager da Kingston no Brasil, Paulo Vizaco. Para ele, a inteligência artificial está indo “para todos os lados”, em meio a uma “uma corrida gigante de players investindo até trilhões de dólares na criação de infraestrutura”. E o Rio Grande do Sul, como região que está recebendo projetos bilionários na área de data centers, como o da Parks, em Cachoeirinha, e o Scala AI City, em Eldorado do Sul, é um local onde há uma atenção concentrada, por meio de oportunidades de parcerias. “Obviamente que vemos monitorando todos esses projetos. Estamos em contato com a maioria deles conversando, vendo o que que a gente pode agregar”, comentou Vizaco. Para ele, a Kingston também acompanha de perto as discussões e iniciativas regulatórias e tributárias no Brasil, a exemplo do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), sancionado a nível no mês passado. Data Center World Brasil 2026 e participação da Kingston no evento Corrida global pela IA acelera Conforme o executivo, a consolidação de incentivos como este é fundamental para reduzir o custo de infraestrutura no Brasil e tornará o ecossistema nacional de data centers ainda mais competitivo frente ao mercado mundial. “Como uma empresa de capital privado, temos a facilidade de se mover muito mais rápido do que qualquer outra. Então nos adaptamos bem a estas condições, principalmente tributárias. Temos uma flexibilidade muito grande neste sentido”, disse ele. O gerente de Tecnologia da Kingston, Iuri Santos, comentou que as empresas de maneira geral têm visto inclusive ideias de voltar a viabilizar grandes projetos de infraestrutura tecnológica, ao verem na Kingston economia, suporte local e qualidade que, eventualmente, seja um gargalo em outros fornecedores. Na visão de Santos, “nunca se produziu tanto semicondutor na história da humanidade”, porque a corrida global pela IA gerou uma demanda sem precedentes por componentes de altíssima velocidade e capacidade. Para ele, os preços destes atingiram um novo patamar global, e é irrealista buscar comparar os orçamentos atuais com os de anos anteriores. “Não devemos olhar para os preços que tínhamos antes, porque aquilo é um mundo sem a IA. A gente mudou, a tecnologia mudou. As empresas que estão ficando para trás são as que ainda estão olhando para o passado em vez de olhar para o presente imaginando se preparar para o futuro. Virou uma questão de sobrevivência: eu preciso me digitalizar”, apontou ele.

artigo.texto: A major improvement for Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), Valeo’s aluminum heat exchanger delivers a 38% increase in cooling capacity, a 25% reduction in electrical consumption, and over a decade of proven corrosion resistance. October 7, 2026 – SAN JOSE, Calif. — At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit 2026 (October 12–15), Valeo will present, with OVH Cloud, the validation status of its breakthrough aluminum heat exchanger technology for data center thermal management. This technology is applicable for the rear door cooling modules of rack or fan wall in the core space of data centers (white space). It represents a paradigm shift in the industry. With over two years of dedicated development in the sector, Valeo is demonstrating its industrial capability and readiness to scale production. Leveraging decades of automotive thermal management, heat exchangers and corrosion know-how, Valeo develops solutions aimed at supporting the AI industry’s exponential scaling needs. Pascale Herman, Data center & BESS Vice President at Valeo, said: “Presenting our ongoing work at OCP 2026 represents an important step in our journey within the data center ecosystem. Over the past two years, we have made significant progress in evaluating how aluminum liquid cooling can meet the rigorous reliability and performance standards required by modern high-density facilities. By combining these early testing metrics with our decades of automotive thermal management expertise, we are working to develop scalable thermal solutions to support the industry’s evolving infrastructure needs responsibly and effectively.” A validated breakthrough for data centers cooling As artificial intelligence (AI) workloads push rack densities to new heights, aluminum heat exchangers are being evaluated to provide a powerful, lightweight, more efficient, and scalable alternative to traditional copper hardware. Valeo’s aluminum solutions deliver a 38% increase in cooling capacity and 65% in power density versus traditional copper solutions, while simultaneously reducing fan electrical consumption by 25%. These validation results establish a clear technological breakthrough, directly optimizing Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE) and Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), ideal for retrofitting existing or for new racks. Automotive-grade reliability: pushing the boundaries of endurance To evaluate long-term feasibility, and directly address industry concerns regarding aluminum corrosion, Valeo has implemented a comprehensive, accelerated long-run testing framework to simulate long-term reliability and OVH Cloud has been running real time and conditions tests for several months. Testing on Valeo’s specific coating has already successfully reached the equivalent of more than 10-years operating life, fully aligning with the standard infrastructure lifespan of the data center industry. Valeo is currently pushing tests up to 15 years ensuring the material unconditionally meets the stringent, long-term lifespan expectations of data center operators. This ongoing research aims to establish a clear pathway toward production-grade aluminum infrastructure for next-generation data centers. A comprehensive liquid cooling vision addressing the data center industry evolution While the aluminum exchanger takes center stage at OCP 2026, it is part of a broader liquid cooling ecosystem engineered to challenge traditional data center thermal limits and address the industry’s rapid evolution. Valeo’s technology portfolio also includes Direct-to-Chip (DLC) systems (both Single-Phase and Two-Phase) for high-density racks, as well as Zero-Water Immersion Units for Micro-Edge compute applications. By applying decades of automotive thermal expertise, stringent quality standards, and a vast global manufacturing footprint in all regions, Valeo brings a new industrial perspective to data center cooling. As accelerating AI demand reshapes digital infrastructure, Valeo combines high-volume production scale with cutting-edge innovation to power the digital transition. About Valeo Valeo is a leading global technology company creating innovative solutions and systems for automotive and technology partners worldwide. Valeo is structured around its POWER, BRAIN and LIGHT Divisions, and Valeo Service, the augmented service partner, for the aftermarket and new forms of mobility. Valeo is committed to making mobility safer, more sustainable and affordable to all. The Group is playing a vital role in shaping the Car of Tomorrow: which will be electrified, safer and software-defined. Valeo is leveraging its global industrial footprint and its technological leadership in electrification, advanced driver assistance systems, lighting and software to capture an increasing share of value per vehicle. Valeo is listed on the Paris Stock Exchange. Valeo in brief: €20.9 billion in sales in 2025 | 100,000 employees worldwide | 29 countries | 149 production plants | 59 R&D centers | 19 distribution platforms (as of February 26, 2026).
