artigo.texto: NY Senate candidates spar over AI data centers, immigration law PLATTSBURGH, N.Y. (WCAX) - Candidates in New York’s 45th Senate District met in a debate on Tuesday, with incumbent Republican Dan Stec facing Glens Falls nurse practitioner and Democrat Melissa Seale ahead of the November election. A panel asked the candidates several questions, including their thoughts on New York’s one-year AI data center moratorium. “If there’s adequate energy there, then why shouldn’t it go forward? That should be a decision that’s made locally and not from Albany, which is why I opposed the moratorium,” Stec said. “The biggest thing is making sure these AI data centers do not impact our communities, the people and the environment,” Seale said. Both candidates also provided their views on statewide immigration policy. Debate panel member Alek LaShomb: Local Cops, Local Crimes Act passed this year that prohibits local law enforcement from working with federal immigration officials on civil investigations. Do you think this legislation goes far enough or would you like to see this peeled back a little bit? Melissa Seale: If we are having our community police officers do the work of immigration, which is a federal program, it’s taking away from our communities and I feel it could make them less safe. Dan Stec: You do not want cops knowing one thing and their brothers and sisters in law enforcement having any ability to work with each other; it’s just unsafe for everybody. Stec and Seale also said they would work to get a constitutional amendment on former state prisons to voters. That proposal would take three vacant state prisons out of the forest preserve and make them available for development. “We have a housing crisis; how can we be creative in utilizing these facilities?” Seale said. While Seale said she doesn’t know how much land should be exchanged for the trio, Stec said he would compromise on a higher amount. Alek LaShomb: If environmentalists say we want more than two thousand acres for all three back into the forest preserve, would you support that? Dan Stec: Yes, I would like to know what exactly we are talking about as far as what 2000 acres that is as I am sure they would, but there’s no magic number for me. Mountain Lake PBS’ full debate airs Friday, Oct. 9 at 8 p.m. You can also watch online and on the PBS app. Election Day is Nov. 3. Copyright 2026 WCAX. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Texas regulators have signed off on a long-debated move away from one of West Texas' thirstiest coal plants. The decision tests whether wind, solar, and battery storage can replace aging fuel-burning infrastructure without sacrificing grid reliability. It carries particular weight in a drought-prone region, where the Tolk plant has depended on the shrinking Ogallala Aquifer and where customers in Texas and New Mexico still rely on steady power. Here's what to know For Southwestern Public Service Company, the ruling means the Tolk coal plant near Lubbock can be retired and replaced with a new resource package: 1,100 megawatts of wind, 189 megawatts of solar, and 322 megawatts of battery storage, as CleanTechnica reported. Across Texas and New Mexico, the company says that combination should produce enough power for roughly 375,000 households. Texas regulators didn't rely on renewables alone. They also signed off on two gas peaker plants in Texas, but only under strict cost caps, allowing the utility to add limited gas backup instead of keeping the older coal plant in service. Josh Smith, a Sierra Club Environmental Law Program attorney who has spent years working on the Tolk plant, said the ruling shows there's "a common-sense path in Texas to transition away from expensive, dirty, thirsty coal. Texas doesn't need coal anymore, even as it prepares for increased demand, and today's decision clearly shows that." He added, "When Tolk closes, it will save abundant water in a drought-prone region, millions of ratepayer dollars, and eliminate millions of tons of harmful pollution every year, making rural West Texas a healthier place to live." The plant's retirement schedule had already been moving forward. SPS, which is owned by Xcel Energy, had previously said Tolk would close by 2032 under a 2020 Sierra Club agreement, then later proposed a December 2028 shutdown, as CleanTechnica reported. Rulings from the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission and Texas regulators set the closure for early 2029. More background Tolk's water demand is enormous. Sierra Club's analysis, Watts Wasting Texas Water, cited by CleanTechnica, said Tolk drew 1.2 billion gallons of groundwater in 2024. In 2015, its water use reached 3.3 billion gallons. Renewable energy uses very little water during operation. Closing the plant could ease pressure on the Ogallala Aquifer, a crucial groundwater source that has been under strain for years, while also reducing pollution tied to coal combustion and transport. The pollution concerns are significant as well. In 2025, Sierra Club figures cited by CleanTechnica said Tolk emitted 3.2 million tons of carbon pollution, along with 5.4 million pounds of nitrogen oxide pollution and 15.5 million pounds of sulfur dioxide. A 2026 Sierra Club health analysis linked the plant to 10 premature deaths each year, mostly in surrounding rural counties. Sierra Club said the closure should also mean fewer open-air rail shipments of coal from Wyoming, reducing coal dust and particle pollution along the route. What's being done? Texas regulators capped costs on the gas peaker plants, while the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission allowed the renewable and gas construction to move forward but, as CleanTechnica reported, didn't rule on the utility's request to classify the new gas-fired power plants as zero-carbon resources. Cyrus Reed, the Legislative and Conservation Director of the Lone Star Chapter of Sierra Club, said the approved replacement mix is the most practical option available. "These solar, wind, and battery storage projects are clearly the most cost-effective and efficient means of replacing the aging and increasingly expensive Tolk coal plant while also maintaining system reliability, saving scarce groundwater resources, utilizing existing transmission rights, and reducing harmful pollution," Reed said. Where can I learn more? These stories follow the same change for Tolk, with utilities leaning on solar and battery storage to replace older plants across the country. • Near Dallas, developers launched a major solar-and-storage buildout to help meet Texas demand. • In Texas, a massive solar farm entered service with 80 MWh of batteries. • In San Antonio, CPS Energy added a massive new battery to back up peak demand. • Duke Energy is turning a massive coal plant overhaul into solar-and-battery capacity. • In Kentucky, regulators approved an unprecedented solar expansion after retiring seven fossil plants. artigo.texto: MAHOMET – Mahomet officials have ended talks with a data center developer after facing backlash from the community, Village President Jason Tompkins announced Monday. Officials had been in talks with Clean Cloud Energy, a data center developer based on the east coast, about a proposal to build a data center in the village as early as January. “I have publicly opposed this project,” Trustee Bruce Colravy said in a statement. “I am proud of those in the community and surrounding area who spent time and energy standing in opposition to it. They have made a difference.” In a press release, officials said questions and concerns from residents played a “significant role” in making this decision. “Our responsibility is to carefully evaluate potential developments and determine whether there is a path forward that serves Mahomet’s interests,” Tompkins said. “Listening to our residents is an essential part of that responsibility.” The press release states officials are still committed to attracting commercial development and expanding the village’s commercial tax base, but they will focus on opportunities that align with the community’s priorities and long-term interests, which does not include data centers. Champaign County currently has a one-year pause on data center development, but it does not apply to development within Mahomet. The data center moratorium ends next spring and was put in place to allow a task force to develop new guidelines for future large-scale projects in the county. Many residents have called for the county to outright ban data centers, but some county officials say they lack the authority to do so without home rule. An effort to put home rule on the November ballot was thwarted in August by a bipartisan group of board members, saying they lacked information to make an informed decision on the issue. State lawmakers have not enacted data center regulations thus far, but Gov. JB Pritzker has called on legislators to take up the issue in the November legislative veto session. In the meantime, he paused the state’s data center tax incentive and released a framework to regulate data centers.

artigo.texto: SP vai esperar regulamento do Redata para rever ICMS de data centers Vice-governador diz que São Paulo não vai mexer no ICMS antes de seis meses, prazo no qual acredita que o decreto regulamentador das isenções federais - sem qualquer relação com os estados - sairá. O vice-governador de São Paulo, Felicio Ramuth, afirmou hoje, 6, na Futurecom 2026, que o estado só deve rever a incidência de ICMS sobre equipamentos para data center após a publicação do decreto federal que regulamentará o Redata. A seu ver, este decreto vai demorar ao menos seis meses para sair. “Não adianta a gente discutir ICMS se o Redata vai acabar com isso”, afirmou durante conversa com jornalistas na Futurecom. Vale lembrar que o Redata mexe em imposto de importação, PIS/Cofins. ICMS é imposto cobrado pelos estados, independentemente dos tributos federais. E no caso dos data centers, ele será incidente pelos próximos cinco anos, ao longo do período de transição da reforma tributária. “Então são medidas, na verdade, paliativas por certo período, porque em cinco anos a gente vai ter a reforma tributária de fato efetiva”, disse. Redata e reforma passam a conviver O regime para data centers procura reduzir custos dos novos projetos. A reforma, por sua vez, altera progressivamente a estrutura de tributação sobre consumo e investimentos. Para o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho, o instrumento utilizado é secundário diante do efeito econômico produzido. “Se vai ser o Redata ou se vai ser reforma tributária, o importante é a gente discutir o benefício”, defendeu. Já o governo paulista enfatiza o caráter transitório de parte dos incentivos e pretende calibrar sua própria política de ICMS depois que as regras federais estiverem definidas.

artigo.texto: DeKalb County considers environmental impact study on data centers DEKALB COUNTY, Ga. - DeKalb County officials are considering a proposal to commission an independent study examining the environmental and health impacts of local data center developments. DeKalb data center proposal What we know: DeKalb County commissioners discussed a proposal Tuesday night at Dunwoody City Hall to bring in a third-party group to evaluate how large data centers impact local land, water and air. Commissioner Ted Terry introduced the measure to ensure health and environmental effects are understood before decisions are made on future developments. The board did not take a vote Tuesday, but members placed the proposal on the agenda for their next full meeting on Tuesday. Community health concerns What they're saying: Some local residents oppose hyperscale facility expansions, raising concerns over water systems, increased power demands and rising residential utility bills. Resident Gina Mangham said the issue centers on resident health, quality of life and rising noise pollution. Resident Rosalind McIntyre warned about heat islands and air pollution. Terry emphasized that he wants to limit the scale of future developments, require renewable energy, ban diesel generators and enforce buffer zones around neighborhoods. Existing development freeze The backstory: DeKalb County currently operates under a moratorium that pauses new data center applications through March. According to Terry, no applications for zoning or building data centers can be received while the moratorium remains active. DeKalb data center study What we don't know: Commissioners have not yet selected an outside firm to conduct the third-party study. It remains unknown whether the board will officially approve funding for the environmental study during their upcoming vote on Tuesday. The Source: The information in this story was gathered from a broadcast report by FOX 5 reporter Christopher King, who covered the DeKalb County Commissioners meeting in Dunwoody, as well as on-record statements from DeKalb County Commissioner Ted Terry and local residents Gina Mangham and Rosalind McIntyre.

artigo.texto: LG Electronics expands chiller production for AI data centers The company plans to invest a total of USD 110 million in a new air-cooled chiller production facility in the US and in expanding two air-cooled chiller production lines in South Korea. LG Electronics (LG) is expanding its chiller manufacturing capabilities with a new production facility in the United States and increased production capacity in South Korea, further strengthening its ability to deliver end-to-end cooling solutions for AI data centers (AIDCs). The company’s new air-cooled chiller production facility in Windsor, Virginia will produce air-cooled chillers for AIDCs, with production scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. The facility’s chiller production will support a stable, responsive supply system for rising demand across North America, while serving as a strategic base for LG’s regional expansion, the company said. LG is also expanding its air-cooled chiller production lines in Pyeongtaek and Changwon, South Korea. The company is improving operational efficiency by adopting a conveyor-based production system designed for mass production. The company plans to invest a total of KRW 150 billion (about USD 110 million) in its new US facility and its factories in Pyeongtaek and Changwon. LG is also broadening its AIDC thermal management business through its Chip-to-Chiller solution strategy. The portfolio includes chillers, Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and cold plates that absorb heat directly from chips. LG is pursuing additional AIDC projects in North America through its relationships with leading hyperscalers and big tech companies. In Asia, LG is applying its “One LG” strategy by combining heating, ventilation and air conditioning technologies with battery solutions and data center design, build and operation capabilities from other LG affiliates. LG is also applying this integrated approach to Sinar Mas Group’s hyperscale AIDC project in Jakarta, Indonesia, the company said. “We will continue to strengthen our core capabilities in AI data center cooling solutions, from differentiated product technologies to production capacity,” said James Lee, president of the LG Eco Solution Company. “With these capabilities, we will ensure a stable supply and actively address rapidly growing market demand.”

artigo.texto: Desperdício de comida agora pode gerar créditos de carbono Nova modalidade de crédito de carbono busca unir redução de emissões, combate ao desperdício de alimentos e segurança alimentar Se uma empresa quiser reduzir sua pegada de carbono, pode comprar créditos de carbono emitidos pela Verra, o maior programa de certificação de créditos de carbono do mundo. Esses créditos podem ser destinados a projetos como energia renovável ou restauração de florestas, permitindo que uma empresa reivindique os benefícios ambientais de um novo parque eólico ou de árvores plantadas em uma área que havia sido desmatada. Agora existe uma nova opção: créditos de carbono para alimentos resgatados, que ajudam a financiar organizações que coletam alimentos que seriam desperdiçados e os distribuem para pessoas necessitadas. Esses créditos emitidos pela Verra agora estão disponíveis graças à Brightly, uma startup de Boston fundada em 2023 por Andy Levitt, que anteriormente fundou e comandou a Purple Carrot, uma empresa de kits de refeições à base de plantas. A Brightly já tem contratos com mais de 25 organizações de resgate de alimentos. Agora, porém, seus créditos de carbono relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos estão sendo emitidos pela Verra, tornando-os os primeiros do tipo dentro da metodologia do padrão de certificação para reduzir a perda e o desperdício de alimentos. Os créditos de carbono são cercados de controvérsias. Pesquisas descobriram que alguns projetos não entregaram benefícios climáticos reais; especialistas afirmam que a possibilidade de usar créditos pode permitir o greenwashing. Levitt sabe que existe desconfiança em relação ao mercado de carbono, mas afirma que a solução da Brightly cria um “ciclo virtuoso de atividade” que financia ainda mais o resgate de alimentos, permitindo que organizações sem fins lucrativos alimentem mais pessoas. “Agora somos capazes de oferecer uma solução inovadora para empresas que querem se concentrar em enfrentar tanto os desafios ambientais quanto a fome”, diz Levitt. “É uma categoria e uma classe completamente novas de créditos de carbono que existem no mercado.” Reduzir o desperdício de alimentos é uma maneira clara de enfrentar as mudanças climáticas. Globalmente, o desperdício de alimentos responde por entre 6% e 10% das emissões mundiais. A aviação, para comparação, responde por cerca de 3%. Ao mesmo tempo, dezenas de milhões de americanos têm acesso limitado ou incerto a alimentos e dependem de bancos de alimentos ou despensas comunitárias para complementar suas compras. A Feeding America estima que cerca de 50 milhões de americanos receberam assistência alimentar de organizações beneficentes em 2023. Muitas dessas organizações, porém, enfrentam dificuldades de financiamento, especialmente diante do aumento da demanda provocado pela alta dos preços dos alimentos e pelo estresse econômico generalizado. ENFRENTANDO O DESAFIO AMBIENTAL E A FOME A Brightly afirma que sua solução enfrenta os dois lados dessa questão. “Nosso objetivo é criar financiamento sustentável para organizações sem fins lucrativos de resgate de alimentos, permitindo que elas mantenham os alimentos fora dos aterros sanitários e alimentem pessoas que passam fome”, diz Levitt. Ao financiar o resgate de alimentos, a Brightly afirma evitar que o metano emitido pelo desperdício de alimentos chegue à atmosfera. Uma parte fundamental de um crédito de carbono eficaz é a adicionalidade, o que significa que a redução das emissões não teria acontecido de qualquer maneira sem a receita gerada pelo crédito de carbono. A Brightly afirma quantificar os benefícios de seus créditos de carbono coletando um histórico de três anos da atividade de uma organização de resgate de alimentos, estabelecendo uma linha de base para o benefício ambiental gerado por aquela organização. A empresa contabiliza apenas o impacto ambiental que excede essa linha de base. Essas organizações sem fins lucrativos coletam todos os tipos de alimentos; algumas podem se concentrar em frutas, legumes e verduras, enquanto outras trabalham com produtos não perecíveis. Cada um desses alimentos tem seu próprio impacto ambiental. A Brightly analisa todos os dados fornecidos pelas organizações sobre o que foi resgatado e em que quantidade, atribuindo um impacto climático a cada tipo de alimento, do pão à carne. “Isso é tratado em um nível hiper específico, linha por linha, alimento por alimento, para alcançar esse grau de precisão e conservadorismo necessário para obter uma classificação de crédito de carbono de alta qualidade”, diz Levitt. Empresas que vão de fabricantes de alimentos a supermercados, e até mesmo companhias de fora do setor alimentício, como empresas de vestuário, poderiam comprar os créditos da Brightly relacionados ao desperdício de alimentos. A Brightly repassa até 80% da receita obtida com a venda dos créditos para as organizações de resgate de alimentos, financiando seus esforços e permitindo que elas ampliem suas operações. É difícil especificar quanto, em dólares, uma organização média de resgate de alimentos poderia receber, diz Levitt, porque os créditos de carbono não são criados individualmente para cada organização; em vez disso, as ações daquela organização representam uma parte de um conjunto maior de créditos. UM IMPACTO HIPERLOCAL A Brightly já analisou mais de 5 bilhões de libras de dados sobre alimentos resgatados, o equivalente a mais de 1 milhão de toneladas métricas de emissões de gases de efeito estufa evitadas. A empresa também já contratou vendas futuras de mais de 80 mil créditos. Com a notícia de que a Verra está emitindo os créditos da Brightly, Levitt espera que esse impacto cresça. A Brightly espera emitir 300 mil créditos por ano, com base em projetos de resgate de alimentos nos Estados Unidos. A empresa também está trabalhando em projetos no exterior. artigo.texto: Propostas de regulamentação sobre captura e armazenamento de carbono associados às operações de petróleo e gás. (Chinhphu.vn) - No projeto de decreto que detalha algumas disposições e medidas para organizar e orientar a implementação da Lei do Petróleo e Gás, o Ministério da Indústria e Comércio propõe regulamentações sobre as atividades de captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS) associadas às operações de petróleo e gás. O Ministério da Indústria e Comércio declarou que as atividades de CCS associadas às operações de petróleo e gás constituem uma nova disposição em comparação com o Decreto nº 45/2023/ND-CP. As regulamentações sobre CCS no Decreto aplicam-se apenas às atividades de CCS associadas às operações de petróleo e gás no âmbito da Lei do Petróleo e Gás; a proteção ambiental, os créditos de carbono, a medição, a comunicação, a avaliação, a certificação das reduções de emissões e outras questões específicas são regidas por leis específicas relevantes. O projeto de Decreto propõe a inclusão de disposições sobre a avaliação e seleção de formações geológicas que armazenam CO₂; a implementação de atividades de CCS no âmbito dos contratos de petróleo e gás; os requisitos técnicos e de segurança para a operação de instalações de CCS; o descomissionamento de instalações de CCS; os custos recuperáveis de projetos de CCS; a receita proveniente de créditos de carbono; e os mecanismos de contabilização. Especificamente: Avaliando o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ A minuta afirma que o relatório que avalia o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ inclui os seguintes conteúdos principais: a) Visão geral da geologia da região, incluindo história tectônica, estrutura geológica e sistemas de falhas; b) Características geológicas e geofísicas da formação geológica que se espera armazenar CO₂; c) Resultados da simulação hidrodinâmica tridimensional do reservatório, incluindo previsões de curto e longo prazo do estado do CO₂ após a injeção; d) Calcule o potencial de armazenamento efetivo em diferentes cenários; d) Avaliar os riscos de vazamento, incluindo a análise do potencial, da probabilidade e das consequências do vazamento, e propor medidas de mitigação; e) Avaliar o impacto das operações de injeção na zona afetada pela pressão, incluindo o impacto nos reservatórios de petróleo e gás adjacentes e nas atividades de petróleo e gás existentes; g) Avaliar os riscos para as pessoas, o ambiente e os recursos relevantes, em conformidade com a lei; h) O estado dos furos de sondagem existentes que penetram a formação do reservatório e as soluções propostas para garantir a sua integridade; i) Conclusões e recomendações sobre a adequação da formação geológica para fins de armazenamento de CO₂. O relatório de avaliação do potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ é um componente do dossiê da proposta de implantação de CCS e é usado como base para o desenvolvimento do plano diretor de implantação de CCS ou do plano de implantação de CCS, conforme estipulado no Artigo 50 da Lei do Petróleo. Os resultados de levantamentos básicos de petróleo e gás, estudos gerais e estudos e avaliações de formações geológicas armazenadoras de CO₂ que tenham sido aprovados e aceitos por agências ou organizações competentes, e que atendam aos requisitos de conteúdo, qualidade e confiabilidade dos documentos, serão herdados e utilizados como base para a elaboração de relatórios sobre a avaliação de formações geológicas armazenadoras de CO₂ e planos de implementação de CCS, conforme estipulado neste Decreto. Implementação de atividades de CCS (Captura e Armazenamento de Carbono) no âmbito de contratos de petróleo e gás. De acordo com a minuta, o contratado propõe adicionar atividades de CCS ao contrato de petróleo e gás com base em um relatório que avalia o potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ e um plano para implementar atividades de CCS, conforme estipulado no Artigo 50 da Lei de Petróleo e Gás. O contratado está autorizado a receber CO₂ gerado por operações de petróleo e gás e outras atividades emissoras para processamento, transporte, injeção e armazenamento no âmbito do contrato de petróleo e gás. A captura de CO₂ em locais de emissão fora das operações de petróleo e gás deverá ser realizada em conformidade com as leis aplicáveis. A elaboração, avaliação e aprovação de alterações aos contratos de petróleo e gás, bem como a emissão de certificados de registo de investimento alterados para adicionar atividades de CCS aos contratos de petróleo e gás, serão realizadas de acordo com as disposições do artigo 18.º da Lei do Petróleo e Gás e do artigo 26.º deste Decreto. Nos casos em que as formações geológicas que armazenam CO₂ ou as zonas afetadas pela pressão se estendam para além da área do contrato de petróleo e gás existente, em blocos abertos adjacentes, a proposta, a avaliação e a aprovação para a expansão da área do contrato para fins de armazenamento de CO₂ serão realizadas de acordo com as disposições da Cláusula 4, Artigo 21 da Lei de Petróleo e Gás e do Artigo 35 deste Decreto. O plano geral de implementação de CCS e o plano de implementação de CCS podem ser incluídos no plano geral de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás, no plano de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás ou em planos de ajuste correspondentes, ou podem ser elaborados separadamente; a elaboração, avaliação e aprovação devem ser realizadas de acordo com os regulamentos pertinentes ao plano geral de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás e ao plano de desenvolvimento do campo de petróleo e gás. O plano de descomissionamento da instalação de CCS é elaborado dentro do plano de descomissionamento da instalação de petróleo e gás, de um plano de ajuste correspondente, ou é preparado separadamente e implementado de acordo com os regulamentos sobre descomissionamento de instalações de petróleo e gás. artigo.texto: By Hank Russell A Florida-based energy company has announced it is suspending operations of two of its battery energy storage systems (BESS) on eastern Long Island. NextEra Energy has agreed to suspend operations at the facility at Cove Hollow Road in East Hampton and the facility in Montauk near Fort Pond. Both facilities are jointly owned by NextEra Energy and National Grid. The suspension follows weeks of discussions between Suffolk County and NextEra. Under the arrangement, NextEra will suspend operations at both sites and remove the Novec 1230 fire suppression agent from both facilities by approximately October 9. “We are very grateful that this agreement has been reached,” said Suffolk County executive Ed Romaine. “The 2023 fire at the East Hampton BESS location, and the consequent contamination of the site and surrounding areas, prove that the operations must cease until changes are made that will protect our drinking water.” The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation has determined that, when water was applied to the East Hampton facility during a May 2023 fire, it mixed with Novec™ 1230 — a chemical agent used for fire suppression — and broke down into PFPrA, a short-chain “forever chemical,” which has since been detected in drinking water in the surrounding area. Two Suffolk County Water Authority (SCWA) wells have been taken offline. The county has drilled monitoring wells to investigate the contamination and supports the SCWA’s litigation against NextEra. In July, Romaine and East Hampton Village Mayor Jerry Larsen sent letters to the chief executives of NextEra Energy and National Grid urging them to suspend operations at the East Hampton facility until the investigation is completed. “We need a remediation plan immediately, one approved by the DEC, so the hard work of cleaning the site can begin,” said Romaine. “The community did not know for years that the 2023 fire had left behind PFPrA. They should not wait any longer for the situation to be addressed.” The county will continue its groundwater testing in the area. Long Island Life & Politics reached out to NextEra and National Grid for comment. NextEra issued the following statement: “We are temporarily ceasing operations at our East Hampton and Montauk battery facilities. We remain committed to working with local and state officials.” National Grid did not respond as of press time.

artigo.texto: Jupiter Wagons Secures 41 MW/102.5 MWh BESS Project from UPCL JEM Energy, in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects, emerged as the L1 bidder for UPCL’s Cluster C tender under the TBCB mechanism. October 06, 2026. By News Bureau Jupiter Wagons (JWL), through its energy business JEM Energy, has won a 41 MW/102.5 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project from Uttarakhand Power Corporation (UPCL), in partnership with Madhav Infra Projects. The partnership emerged as the L1 bidder for Cluster C of UPCL's tender, which was conducted under the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism. The projects envisage supply and commissioning of approximately INR 100 crore of BESS system. JWL has also received the formal Letter of Award (LoA) from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company (WBSEDCL) for the 50 MW/200 MWh standalone BESS project at the Jeerat 132 kV substation in North 24 Parganas, West Bengal. The project was secured in August 2026. These developments follow the Union Cabinet's approval of Green Energy Corridor Phase-3, which was welcomed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The scheme provides for 50 GWh of battery energy storage alongside stronger intra-state transmission networks. Substation-level storage of the kind being deployed in Uttarakhand and West Bengal is central to this framework, and JEM Energy is building its utility-scale portfolio in line with it. Speaking on the development, Vivek Lohia, Managing Director, Jupiter Wagons, said, "Winning the Uttarakhand project and receiving the formal award for Jeerat are important steps in building JEM Energy into a scalable energy storage business. With the approval of Green Energy Corridor Phase-3, battery storage is now firmly part of how India will plan and strengthen its grid, and substation-level projects such as these are where that work begins. We reiterate our target of building a BESS order book of approximately INR 1,000 crore by FY27. As the business scales, we expect Jupiter Electric Mobility (JEM) to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and to turn profitable by FY28. We will continue to bid with discipline for utility-scale and Commercial and Industrial (C&I) opportunities across India." The Uttarakhand win takes JEM Energy's presence into a new state. It also strengthens JWL's position in the energy transition ecosystem, in line with the Company's strategy of expanding into high-growth businesses beyond its traditional railway and mobility operations. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: Raleigh leaders could decide Tuesday night whether to pause future data center development in the city. A public hearing will be held Tuesday at 7 p.m. during the Raleigh City Council meeting. Citizens will have a chance to share their opinions on whether the city should approve a six-month pause on data centers before a possible vote. Other WRAL Top Stories A moratorium is a pause, not a ban, on data centers. The conversation started months ago when the city of Raleigh received an application for a large data center on Jones Sausage Road. Raleigh is currently the largest city in North Carolina without a moratorium on data centers. Several cities and counties, including Apex, Durham, Greensboro and Charlotte, have approved similar pauses on data center development. Raleigh already has smaller data centers, but the proposed moratorium would be for large-scale data centers that raise concerns about noise, energy and water use. Raleigh Mayor Janet Cowell previously said the city has to protect its residents while maintaining its status as an innovative city. "We definitely want to protect those that are already operating and not disrupt existing research and development or companies that have located here," Cowell said. "Then we want to have a very rational and careful approach that protects individuals who live in Raleigh and still be known as a tech, innovative city." At last month's Raleigh City Council meeting, some people expressed their support for a moratorium. “When new technology develops, policy usually lags behind, and a moratorium gives you a chance to put a pause on that [and] figure out how to handle this thing," said Laura Harris, a Raleigh resident. Data centers, which support AI computing, are packed with graphics processing units, or GPUs, that generate significantly more heat than traditional computing equipment and often require large amounts of water to cool.

artigo.texto: Solid-state batteries have long been heralded as the next great leap in energy storage, promising to replace the flammable liquid electrolytes inside today’s lithium-ion cells with solid materials that could make devices safer and more energy dense. Yet a persistent engineering problem has slowed their progress: the solid materials that shuttle lithium ions between electrodes are often stiff and unforgiving, struggling to maintain the intimate contact with electrode surfaces that a working battery demands. Now, researchers at Rice University have taken an unusually elegant approach to that problem by asking a question that most electrolyte designers have overlooked — what if the material that carries the ions could also bend, flex, and adapt mechanically to the environment inside a cell? The Rice team, drawn from the departments of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Chemistry, and Materials Science and Nanoengineering, along with the Rice Advanced Materials Institute, has developed a relatively soft and flexible porous material that selectively transports lithium ions. The work, published in the peer-reviewed journal Chemical Science, introduces a new design philosophy for porous solid electrolytes, one that treats mechanical adaptability not as an afterthought but as a core performance criterion, sitting alongside ionic conductivity and chemical stability in the designer’s toolkit. The material at the heart of the study is called ZnBTCA, and it belongs to a family of compounds known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. These are porous crystalline materials built from metal atoms connected by organic molecules into repeating, lattice-like structures. What makes MOFs so compelling for battery applications is their architecture: they contain tiny, ordered channels whose size and chemistry can be tailored to move or hold specific molecules and ions. In principle, a MOF can act as a molecular sieve for charge, allowing lithium ions to stream through its pores while blocking everything else. Many MOFs previously explored as battery electrolytes, however, have been constructed from relatively rigid aromatic linkers — the organic struts that connect the metal nodes — which produce frameworks that are stiff and mechanically unyielding. ZnBTCA takes a fundamentally different route. Instead of an aromatic linker, it employs a flexible aliphatic linker, an organic molecule with a pliable carbon-chain backbone. That single design choice ripples through the entire material: the framework itself becomes softer and more mechanically adaptable, capable of deforming and conforming rather than resisting. The researchers also emphasized practicality in their selection of building blocks. The material is assembled from relatively abundant, low-cost components, including zinc — one of the most accessible metals in the battery chemist’s repertoire — and an inexpensive aliphatic linker, an important consideration if such materials are ever to move from the laboratory bench toward real-world manufacturing. First author Zina Deriche, a graduate student in chemical and biomolecular engineering at Rice, framed the shift in thinking that underpins the work. MOF electrolytes, she noted, are often designed primarily around how effectively they transport ions. The Rice study demonstrates that the mechanical properties of the framework can also be an important part of the design equation. It is a deceptively simple reframing, but one with significant consequences: a material that can flex with the battery as it charges and discharges may hold up better over thousands of cycles than one that cracks or delaminates under mechanical stress. The dual functionality of ZnBTCA is what excites the team most. The material’s flexible molecular building blocks make it relatively soft, while its negatively charged framework structure favors the movement of positively charged lithium ions through its channels. Stavroula Alina Kampouri, a corresponding author of the study and assistant professor across chemical and biomolecular engineering, chemistry, and materials science and nanoengineering, described the convergence of these properties as the most thrilling aspect of the result. The same material, she explained, brings together flexible building blocks that make the framework softer and more adaptable with a negatively charged structure that promotes selective lithium-ion transport. Bringing those properties together, she said, offers a new way to design MOF electrolytes by considering how ions move and how the material behaves mechanically at the same time. The experimental results lend strong support to the design concept. The researchers first exchanged the sodium ions residing within the framework for lithium ions, a process known as ion exchange that is common in MOF chemistry. After the exchange, they found that roughly 95 percent of the mobile charge-balancing ions in the material were lithium, while the framework itself remained structurally intact — a critical demonstration that the delicate crystalline lattice could survive the swapping of its guest ions without collapsing. Selectivity matters enormously in an electrolyte: a material that carries only lithium ions, rather than a mixed crowd of mobile species, delivers cleaner, more efficient battery operation and helps prevent parasitic reactions that degrade performance over time. Further electrochemical testing quantified just how selective the material is. In measurements of the current flowing through the material, lithium ions accounted for approximately 79 percent of the total ionic current — a high lithium-ion transference number that indicates the framework’s channels and charged surfaces are indeed preferentially shepherding lithium rather than the counterions left behind by the exchange process. artigo.texto: Principais Conclusões - As ações da Microsoft ganharam 37,5% no terceiro trimestre, e Jim Cramer diz que a empresa está "começando a recuperar seu investimento monstruoso em data centers". - O retorno está aparecendo na receita da Microsoft, mas seu fluxo de caixa livre caiu por dois anos consecutivos, então a recuperação está apenas começando. - Os gastos de capital da Microsoft subiram de US$ 23,9 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2022 para US$ 116 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, e 30 milhões de usuários do Copilot não podem cobrir essa conta sozinhos. - O ponto a ser observado é se os gastos atingem o pico enquanto a receita continua subindo em direção aos US$ 467 bilhões que os analistas esperam para o ano fiscal de 2028. No episódio de quarta-feira à noite do Mad Money, Jim Cramer, da CNBC, revisou tudo o que preocupava os investidores em junho, no início do que tem sido uma corrida incrível para a Microsoft (MSFT). Desaceleração do Azure. Muito envolvimento com a OpenAI. Clientes que supostamente não pagariam pelo Copilot. "Todas essas preocupações acabaram sendo ou erradas ou falsas", disse ele. Mas Cramer guardou o que chamou de "a maior mudança" para o final: "A Microsoft está começando a recuperar seu investimento monstruoso em data centers." Se ele estiver certo, isso muda tudo. Quão monstruoso estamos falando? O CapEx da Microsoft quase quintuplicou em quatro anos, de US$ 23,9 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2022 para US$ 116 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, o ano até junho… Só esse último ano foi um aumento em relação aos US$ 64,6 bilhões do ano anterior. Se é que dá para dizer, eu diria que "monstruoso" é pouco. (Claro, se você quiser se aprofundar... como meu colega explicou na terça-feira, há uma manobra contábil por trás de como os números de capex da Microsoft são relatados, o que vale a pena ler.) O argumento de Cramer para o retorno começa com o Copilot, que tem "30 milhões de usuários e crescendo. Eles estão pagando." A Microsoft claramente quer muito mais usuários do Copilot também. Na sexta-feira passada, o CEO Satya Nadella anunciou "nossa maior atualização do Copilot até hoje", apresentando-o como "um novo sistema operacional para o trabalho que abrange todos os modelos, todos os fatores de forma e todas as tarefas". O que soa bem, mas obviamente não é suficiente para justificar os gastos com capex. Pelo menos ainda não. A receita está aparecendo Mas, ao ampliar o foco do Copilot para toda a empresa, o retorno fica muito mais fácil de ver… A receita cresceu de US$ 245 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2024 para US$ 332 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, e os cerca de 50 analistas que cobrem a ação esperam US$ 391 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2027 e US$ 467 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2028. Esse é um crescimento sólido, mas, mais importante, desafia uma lei da gravidade: empresas desse tamanho não deveriam acelerar, mas é exatamente isso que o Wall Street espera que a Microsoft faça. Com a receita da Microsoft Cloud subindo 27% ano a ano no último trimestre (e o Azure subindo 43% – e ultrapassando US$ 100 bilhões pela primeira vez!) – há todos os motivos para pensar que tal aceleração é possível. E só é possível graças à expansão dos data centers. Agora, Cramer está um pouco mais confiante do que eu. Ele acha que os gastos com data centers "podem estar até mesmo atingindo o pico e a lucratividade está à vista", e que Nadella e a CFO Amy Hood sabiam que "esses data centers durarão muito mais tempo do que as pessoas pensavam". Se o capex se estabilizar enquanto a receita se capitaliza na taxa que os analistas esperam, o fluxo de caixa livre finalmente deve começar a subir. Essa é a aposta que os investidores fizeram neste trimestre. Então, sim, o investimento monstruoso da Microsoft está começando a dar retorno, pelo menos na linha de cima. Claro, nada nesses gráficos mostra o capex atingindo o pico ainda, e os US$ 116 bilhões do ano fiscal de 2026 são a maior conta até agora. Então, qual é o valor real da ação da Microsoft? artigo.texto: As ações da LG Electronics registravam forte valorização no pregão desta terça-feira (6) após a companhia fechar um novo contrato plurianual para o fornecimento de sistemas de resfriamento de grande porte (chillers) a data centers focados em inteligência artificial (IA) nos Estados Unidos. A operação reforça o reposicionamento da sul-coreana de eletrônicos de consumo no mercado B2B de gestão térmica para infraestrutura crítica de dados. A subsidiária da empresa nos EUA firmou um acordo de longo prazo com a AIR Control Concepts, plataforma de data centers sediada na Virgínia. A parceria prevê o fornecimento de soluções de refrigeração para instalações que somam mais de 5 gigawatts de capacidade computacional. Embora os valores financeiros não tenham sido revelados, a LG destacou que o contrato consolida sua entrada na cadeia de suprimentos de infraestrutura essencial para IA na América do Norte. A reação dos investidores foi imediata. Na Bolsa de Seul, os papéis da LG Electronics chegaram a subir 8,8% no início da sessão, registrando a maior alta diária em cerca de dois meses. A valorização reflete o otimismo com a diversificação de receitas da companhia para além de eletrodomésticos e telas, aproveitando o boom global de demanda por capacidade de processamento intensivo. Para dar conta do volume de pedidos, a LG anunciou planos de expansão capacidade fabril nos Estados Unidos e na Coreia do Sul. A empresa construirá uma nova planta industrial na Virgínia focada no atendimento ao mercado norte-americano, com início de operações previsto para o primeiro semestre de 2027. Em paralelo, a produção será ampliada nas unidades sul-coreanas de Changwon e Pyeongtaek. Além dos contratos norte-americanos, a divisão HVAC (aquecimento, ventilação e ar-condicionado) da empresa vem conquistando espaço em projetos de infraestrutura corporativa no Oriente Médio e na Indonésia. A LG projeta que as novas encomendas anuais de resfriamento para data centers alcancem múltiplos bilhões de dólares até o encerramento de 2026, impulsionadas pelos US$ 426 milhões já garantidos no primeiro semestre do ano. Com o ritmo acelerado de fechamento de negócios, a gestão da companhia afirmou que deve superar antecipadamente a meta estipulada para 2027, que previa R$ US$ 680 milhões em faturamento anual exclusivo na unidade de chillers.

During the 2026-2027 period, Vietnam will focus on building a foundation in terms of institutions, data, technical standards, and a blue classification system; promoting investment opportunities and developing an efficient carbon market. Vietnam is gradually laying the groundwork for a truly functioning carbon market, while simultaneously transforming climate change response goals into drivers for green transition and sustainable development. Notably, to lay the groundwork for the carbon market to "take off," the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment recently issued Decision No. 3696/QD-BNNMT implementing Decision No. 505/QD-TTg of the Prime Minister on the National Digital Transformation Day 2026; which stipulates the completion of the construction and operation of the National Registration System for Greenhouse Gas Emission Quotas and Carbon Credits before October 10, 2026. Building a solidlegal foundation According to Mr. Nguyen Hung Minh, Deputy Head of the Carbon Market Department, Climate Change Agency, greenhouse gases and the greenhouse effect are the core causes of global warming and lead to many consequences of climate change such as rising sea levels and extreme weather events. In Vietnam, the average annual temperature across the country between 1961 and 2023 has been recorded as increasing by approximately 0.2 degrees Celsius per decade. Notably, Vietnam ranks 10th in the world in terms of climate change risk in 2024. Faced with these challenges, Vietnam's system of policies and laws on climate change response has been gradually improved over time, from guidelines, laws, decrees, decisions, and circulars to international agreements and treaties. Among these, Resolution 24-NQ/TW dated June 3, 2013, on proactively responding to climate change, strengthening resource management and environmental protection; Resolution 120/NQ-CP of 2017 on sustainable development of the Mekong Delta adapting to climate change; and Government Resolution 06/NQ-CP promulgating the Action Program to continue implementing Resolution 24-NQ/TW, are fundamental policy decisions. By 2026, the focus will continue to be on building databases, early warning systems for natural disasters, developing a circular economy , efficient resource utilization, and a carbon market. However, climate change provisions are currently regulated in different laws. In particular, the 2020 Environmental Protection Law is a crucial legal foundation for responding to climate change. Specifically, Article 139 of the 2020 Environmental Protection Law provides the legal basis for organizing and developing a carbon market. This forms the fundamental basis for building a carbon market in Vietnam. Looking ahead, Mr. Minh stated that Vietnam will continue to improve its climate change legislation, including researching and proposing the development of a Climate Change Law; reviewing relevant regulations in the 2020 Environmental Protection Law; perfecting technical standards and regulations; promoting the circular economy and green transition; and strengthening the dissemination and popularization of the law. artigo.texto: Specialist investment firm Adaptogen Capital is targeting a €1 billion ($1.61 billion) investment opportunity across European battery energy storage system (BESS) markets by 2030. As part of the company’s approach, it is exploring capital raisings for 2027. The funds would help finance its initial European BESS assets, with an estimated requirement of €260 million in equity and €500 million in debt. The company has developed a 1.2-gigawatt pipeline of Belgian BESS opportunities, with five initial projects in development and progressing towards final investment decisions. Through its operating platform MVA Energy, Adaptogen Capital aims to address grid congestion and the integration of growing renewable generation, alongside a parallel German pipeline. Adaptogen has also progressed a further 500-megawatt (MW) portfolio across two sites in Germany, located at key offshore wind high-voltage landing points on the transmission grid. Adaptogen Capital Managing Director James Mills says grids across Europe are under growing pressure from the pace of renewable buildout, creating a clear investment case for well-located, grid-scale battery storage with firm connections, backed by structured revenue and debt facilities. “We have spent the past three years building a pipeline that targets that opportunity, and our approach of committing capital once projects have reached final investment decision allows infrastructure investors to back assets where development risks have already been substantially reduced,” Mills says. Going beyond the UK Adaptogen’s European ambitions build directly on its UK experience. The company’s original fund, which closed in 2023, has been fully committed to developing and operating BESS assets through Varco Energy, with a follow-on co-investment raised in 2025. Varco Energy’s operational projects include Native River — the UK’s longest-duration transmission-connected battery installation — and Sizing John Phase One. Native River, located south of Liverpool, has a system capacity of 57MW and 138MW hours. It delivers grid-balancing services such as frequency regulation, reserve capacity, and load shifting to support renewable energy integration. The phase-one Sizing John Project is located near St Helens and supports NESO in operating the Mersey Ring. The project is designed to allow for potential expansion as grid demand grows. Adaptogen Capital says that investor appetite for European battery energy storage is strengthening and growing grid constraints reinforce the role of storage as critical energy infrastructure. With few specialist BESS managers operating at scale across Europe, the company says its project-led approach is well aligned with the needs of infrastructure investors seeking exposure to a key asset class in the next phase of the energy transition. Write to Aaliyah Rogan at Mining.com.au Main image: Adaptogen Capital

artigo.texto: HDOT, Sustainability Partners and Hensel Phelps Mark the Start of Construction on Oʻahu and Kauaʻi Microgrids with PV, BESS and Charging Infrastructure The State of Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation (HDOT), Sustainability Partners (SP), and Hensel Phelps have marked the start of construction on new microgrid projects on Oʻahu and Kauaʻi that include solar PV canopies, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicle charging stations. Construction Hawaiian Blessing ceremonies commemorating the start of construction were held in August. The projects are designed to strengthen energy resilience at critical HDOT facilities by integrating solar generation with battery energy storage and intelligent microgrid controls to manage energy generation, storage, and use. Together, the projects are expected to generate 2.2 MWh of renewable energy each day and will include two 1 MW battery energy storage systems. The microgrids are part of HDOT’s broader work to modernize HDOT’s infrastructure and advance the state’s clean energy and resilience goals. “These projects represent another important step in strengthening the resiliency of Hawaiʻi’s infrastructure,” said Ed Sniffen, Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation Director. “These PV and battery storage systems provide critical energy security for our teams during severe weather and multi-day blackouts.” Oʻahu The Oʻahu microgrid will serve HDOT Highways’ Oʻahu District Main Office Facility on Kakoi Street. The project includes a 1 MW battery energy storage system and solar PV canopies expected to generate 1.5 MWh of renewable energy per day. This site will include over 40 Level 2 Chargers and 1 Dual-Port 200 kW DC Fast Charger. Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure microgrid technology will provide the intelligent control layer that coordinates solar generation, battery storage, EV charging, and interaction with the utility grid to optimize how energy is generated, stored, and used. SP is also working with Hawaiian Electric toward enrollment in its Energy Export program, which would allow the site to export surplus power back to the electric grid. Kauaʻi The Kauaʻi microgrid will serve HDOT Highways’ Kauaʻi District Main Office Facility on Haleukana Street. The project includes a 1 MW battery energy storage system and solar PV canopies expected to generate 700 kWh of renewable energy per day. This site will include over 12 Level 2 Chargers and 1 Dual-Port 200 kW DC Fast Charger. As on Oʻahu, Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure microgrid technology will provide centralized visibility and intelligent control of the site’s distributed energy resources, helping coordinate generation, storage, and electrical loads. Hensel Phelps is leading construction of both projects and has worked alongside HDOT and Sustainability Partners on transportation and energy infrastructure throughout Hawaiʻi.

artigo.texto: The voluntary carbon market (VCM) continued to move away from a volume-driven model in the third quarter of 2026, with carbon credit retirements falling even as buyers spent more on the credits they purchased. - Carbon credit retirements reached 30.6 million in Q3 2026, down 9% from 33.7 million a year earlier, according to carbon market data provider Sylvera. However, the value of those retirements rose to $211.8 million from $190.6 million in Q3 2025. The difference points to a market where buyers are becoming more selective. The report reveals that the average price paid for a retired credit climbed to $6.92 in Q3, compared with $5.66 a year earlier. For the first nine months of 2026, the average reached $6.12, up from $5.40 during the same period in 2025. The trend also builds on what Sylvera identified earlier this year. In the first half of 2026, retirement volumes were down 9% year over year, while market value increased. By the end of Q3, however, cumulative retirements had edged above 2025 levels at 130.3 million credits, compared with 129.1 million through the first three quarters of last year. Meanwhile, year-to-date retirement value reached $798 million, 14% above the $697.3 million recorded a year earlier. Quality Is Taking a Bigger Role in Carbon Credit Pricing The strongest signal from the latest data comes from the widening gap between higher- and lower-quality credits. Credits rated BBB or higher represented only 18% of rated retirement volume in Q3. Yet they generated 42% of rated market value. This suggests buyers are willing to pay significantly more for credits that meet stronger quality expectations rather than simply purchasing the cheapest available supply. The premium becomes even clearer across individual project categories. - For afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR), BBB+ credits averaged $23.47 per tonne in Q3, compared with $12.80 for credits rated BB or below. Improved forest management (IFM) showed a similar divide. BBB+ IFM credits reached $21.07, while lower-rated credits averaged $12.79. - REDD+ also saw a sharp quality-driven price difference. BBB+ REDD+ credits averaged $7.75 in Q3, up 58% from $4.90 a year earlier. Lower-rated REDD+ credits increased from $2.70 to $3.56 over the same period. As a result, the REDD+ price gap between the two quality groups nearly doubled from $2.20 to $4.19. The trend suggests that buyers are not abandoning nature-based credits altogether. Instead, they appear increasingly willing to distinguish between projects based on perceived quality. - RELATED: Carbon Credit Prices Explained: What Determines the Value of a Carbon Credit? - LIVE PRICES: Carbon Credit Prices Today 2026 | Live Chart, EU ETS & VCM Renewables Still Dominate, But Their Market Position Is Changing Renewable energy projects accounted for 41% of Q3 retirements, giving them the largest share among project categories. However, Sylvera cautions that the increase in market share does not represent renewed growth in renewable credit demand. Renewable retirements totaled 40.7 million credits during the first nine months of 2026, roughly unchanged from the same period in 2025. That remains far below the 77.1 million credits retired during the first three quarters of 2022. Full-year renewable retirements peaked at 99.7 million in 2022 before falling to 49.3 million in 2025. The quality issue is particularly important here. Sylvera does not rate renewable projects above C because many grid-connected renewable projects face additionality concerns. As a result, renewables accounted for 76% of B/C/D-rated retirement volume in Q3. That helped push the share of B/C/D-rated credits across the entire retirement market to 66.1%, the highest level since Q3 2023. In other words, renewable credits continue to provide substantial market volume, but their presence also weighs on the overall quality profile of retirements. REDD+ Demand Normalizes While Agriculture Gains Ground REDD+ accounted for 18% of Q3 retirements, down sharply from 38% in Q2. However, the comparison needs context because Q2’s unusually high share was largely driven by one major retirement. Beyond that temporary spike, REDD+ demand appears relatively stable, with retirement activity spread across Colombia, Brazil, Cambodia, Peru, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Agriculture was a more notable growth area. Its share of retirements increased from 2.55% to 7.82%, while retirement volume more than doubled. Energy and utility companies played an important role in that shift, with agriculture representing 28% of their Q3 retirement mix, compared with 6.8% a year earlier. This diversification matters because the market is gradually moving beyond a small group of traditional project categories. Buyers are showing greater interest in credits tied to agriculture, forest management, and other project types where measurable climate and environmental benefits can support stronger pricing. Corporate Buyers Are Still Active Despite the overall decline in quarterly retirement volumes, major corporate buyers continued to transact at scale. Yamato Transport and Corpay each retired about 2 million credits in Q3, making them the largest retirees during the quarter. Primax Colombia followed with just over 1 million. For the first nine months of 2026, Eni remained the largest retiree with nearly 9 million credits. TASC, Organización Terpel, Engie and Lenovo also ranked among the largest buyers. At the same time, Shell’s retreat remains significant. The company retired only about 496,000 credits through the first three quarters of 2026, compared with roughly 7 million during the same period in 2025. artigo.texto: Data centers are preventing a US recession, NMSU economist says Despite a weak housing market, data center growth has buoyed the US economy, New Mexico State University economics professor Chris Erickson tells KOAT. Data centers are preventing the U.S. from falling into a recession, a New Mexico State University economic expert told KOAT on Saturday. "Data centers are keeping the economy growing at this point; they are the main drivers of the economy," said Chris Erickson, a professor of economics at NMSU. RELATED: Data centers become key issue in New Mexico governor’s race "Its investment in data centers has kept the economy buoyed up. The housing sector has been quite weak for a while. Usually when the housing sector is that weak, you can expect either slowdown or even a recession to follow that because construction is such an important source of jobs. But because the data centers have taken up all the slack in construction, that hasn't happened," Erickson explained. Data center growth in New Mexico is not uncontroversial, and Erickson said he believes there could be a slowdown in new data center development. The controversy surrounding them might make it difficult for companies to secure funding for new projects, he said. Three New Mexico counties have placed moratoriums on data center development, and a fourth is currently considering one. Democratic lawmakers in Santa Fe are proposing a statewide moratorium for the 2027 legislative session. Opponents are wary of the environmental impacts and financial costs of data centers. Still, there are major data centers currently operating or in development across the state, including an operational Meta data center in Valencia County and a major Oracle data center under construction in Doña Ana County. Google is also exploring a potential site in Lea County.

artigo.texto: Wisconsin Policy Forum Data centers can deliver multi-billion-dollar investments and large numbers of jobs to Wisconsin communities. But key issues around their development remain unresolved, including how to ensure residents are spared from increases to transmission rates or property taxes. Far from being a hub of data center construction, a new Wisconsin Policy Forum report finds Wisconsin lags states such as Virginia and Ohio in both the number and size of its data centers. Still, three major hyperscale data centers are being built in Wisconsin in recent years, with more being proposed and often facing significant opposition. A Microsoft data center is up and running in Mount Pleasant, while centers are under construction in Port Washington and Beaver Dam. Recent technological advancements in artificial intelligence are driving a national data center boom. A broader examination of the impacts of this technology — an understandably salient issue for many — is beyond the scope of this report. Instead, our report seeks to ground discussions in facts about how they affect local government finances, the regional economy, the energy grid, and more. For example, due in large part to these centers, the latest state projections show peak power demand in Wisconsin is expected to increase by more than 5 gigawatts between 2024 and 2030. This raises the question of who will pay for the added capacity to serve these centers. Electricity arguably represents the single biggest challenge for large data centers– and the single biggest issue for policymakers, our report finds. In considering data center proposals, elected officials have a difficult balance to strike. An August Marquette University Law School poll found 78% of registered voters in Wisconsin felt the costs of large data centers outweigh their benefits, while only 21% felt their benefits outweighed their costs. Some Wisconsin communities have recently blocked construction of large data centers, either by rejecting a specific proposal or approving a blanket moratorium. One of the implications of this is that local officials may have leverage in negotiating data center deals with developers, since there is a credible risk that these proposals will be rejected. The Forum reviewed deals between data center developers and the communities of Mount Pleasant, Port Washington, and Beaver Dam, as well as in two communities where centers were proposed but later canceled: Janesville and DeForest. In general, we found communities were striking reasonable deals that included fiscal safeguards. However, state law makes it challenging for local officials to protect existing taxpayers in the case of data center developments that require significant tax increment finance (TIF) spending on infrastructure or developer incentives. Under current law, there could be initial tax increases on existing property owners — despite the possibility that once the TIF district closes, residents’ taxes could decline to what they were prior to the data center or even less. In addition, most states offer a state sales tax exemption to data centers, as Wisconsin does. While other industries such as manufacturing receive similar treatment here, the cost of these forgone tax revenues is significant. Our report concludes by offering a menu of options for state and local policymakers to consider in response to issues highlighted in our report. Click here to read the full report and learn more. This information is a service of the Wisconsin Policy Forum, the state’s leading resource for nonpartisan state and local government research and civic education. Learn more at wispolicyforum.org

artigo.texto: BYD puts battery cells directly in cooling liquid in new patent BYD has filed an invention patent application describing a battery cabinet that separates its electrical equipment from a lower compartment where cell modules are submerged in dielectric fluid. The design centres on a relatively simple question with significant consequences for an immersion-cooled battery system: how do electrical connections cross the boundary between a dry compartment and a liquid-filled one? Published by the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) on October 5, 2026, as CN 122868832 A, the application covers battery cabinets and energy storage equipment. Filed in March 2025, it describes a two-chamber enclosure in which the cooling medium surrounds the cell modules while electrical equipment remains outside the liquid volume. Why immersion cooling changes the battery enclosure Many contemporary battery systems use indirect liquid cooling. Coolant circulates through aluminium cold plates positioned against the battery modules, with heat passing through the cell casing and intervening materials before reaching the coolant. Immersion cooling changes that arrangement. Instead of bringing coolant to a separate cooling plate, the battery modules sit directly in a non-conductive dielectric fluid. Heat can therefore transfer from the wetted surfaces of the modules directly into the surrounding fluid. The arrangement shortens the thermal path between the battery and the cooling medium, but it also changes the enclosure problem. The liquid must be contained, while electrical components and connection points that are not intended to operate in the fluid must remain isolated from it. That boundary is where BYD’s patent application focuses. Production battery systems still rely on indirect cooling. The distinction is easier to see against BYD and CATL’s existing production architectures. BYD’s MC Cube energy storage system integrates Blade batteries using its cell-to-system architecture, while the MC Cube-T specifies liquid cooling. CATL’s EnerOne and EnerC storage systems likewise use liquid cooling, with cooling plates positioned outside the battery modules. CATL’s Qilin passenger-vehicle battery uses a different packaging arrangement, integrating a liquid-cooling plate into a multifunctional interlayer positioned between adjacent cells. These systems keep the cooling medium in a defined thermal path rather than surrounding the battery modules directly. BYD’s new filing describes another arrangement: the cell modules occupy the liquid-filled chamber itself, while electrical equipment is kept in a separate dry chamber. The resulting engineering problem is not simply how to transfer heat. It is how to maintain an electrical connection across a liquid-tight boundary. BYD routes the connections through the top CN 122868832 A divides the cabinet into two isolated chambers: - Chamber 1: An upper dry compartment containing electrical equipment components. - Chamber 2: A lower liquid compartment containing cell modules submerged in dielectric fluid. The connection between the two chambers is routed through the upper portion of the liquid compartment. Rather than bringing the electrical and signal leads through the floor or side walls of the wet chamber, the design directs them upward before they enter the dry compartment. Location matters because hydrostatic pressure increases with liquid depth. A sealing interface positioned higher in the chamber therefore experiences less hydrostatic pressure than an equivalent interface positioned deeper in the liquid. The electrical equipment remains outside the liquid volume while maintaining the connection to the submerged battery modules. In other words, the filing does not rely solely on the fluid’s cooling dielectric properties to separate the battery’s thermal and electrical environments. It also uses the cabinet’s physical layout to keep the electrical connection points above the main liquid volume. The filing is about a cabinet, not a new vehicle battery The application covers battery cabinets and energy storage equipment and does not identify a passenger vehicle application. It specifies dielectric fluid, including hydrocarbon- or ester-based formulations, rather than standard liquid coolant. The filing therefore describes an immersion-cooled stationary battery enclosure with a dry electrical compartment and a wet battery compartment. That distinction matters because a patent application is not evidence that the architecture has entered production. The application remains under substantive examination, and BYD has not announced commercial production plans for the design. For now, CN 122868832 A documents an enclosure architecture and a specific way of routing electrical connections through the boundary between its dry and liquid-filled sections.

artigo.texto: Old Town became the second Greater Bangor community to pass a short-term ban on data centers Monday. The six-month ban, which outlaws the development of data centers in the city’s industrial zones, is retroactive to Sept. 8, when the Old Town City Council first discussed the possibility of a ban. Data center developments are already not allowed in other zones, according to the city’s land use ordinance. Communities across Maine have passed moratoriums, or temporary bans, on data center developments this year due to the limited knowledge of how they will affect municipalities. The bans, which are generally set to last six months, give towns time to learn about the technology and draft laws to regulate its development. The Old Town City Council passed the ban unanimously at its Monday meeting. Due to extensive conversation about a possible ban during a September meeting, discussion on the ban Monday lasted for about one minute. “I think that our conversation last time was pretty substantial and overarching, and as previously stated, it gives us plenty of time to adequately assess the risks and benefits and pros and cons of all that this super complex, super new thing entails,” Councilor Zachary Wyles said. Residents reached out to councilors before the ban was proposed to say they didn’t want a data center to come to Old Town. Old Town could be a desirable location for a data center because of its history with businesses like Nine Dragons Paper and Old Town Canoe, and its industrial zones, Council President Christian Pushor said at the Sept. 8 meeting. Councilors previously said a long-term ban in the form of zoning changes would be sent to a public referendum to allow voters to decide. The next possible election date would be June 2027. The six-month ban is set to expire in March, but an extension to June could be approved. “I feel like this is such a hot topic that I would like it to go to the public instead of relying on people who have the time and energy to contact us,” Councilor Katrina Wynn said on Sept. 8.

artigo.texto: 43 proposed power plants needed to fuel data centers listed across NEPA PHILADELPHIA (WOLF) — A new environmental report warning about Pennsylvania’s expected growth in natural-gas power generation comes as proposed power plants are already listed across much of northeastern and central Pennsylvania. PennEnvironment Research & Policy Center and Frontier Group project Pennsylvania could add 4.4 gigawatts of natural-gas capacity by the end of 2030, an increase of nearly 15% over the state’s existing gas footprint. The groups say growing demand from data centers is a major driver behind the proposed expansion. A separate Track Data Centers listing provided to FOX56 identifies 43 proposed power plants across the station’s coverage area. Lackawanna County has the largest number, with 15 proposals and 4.8 gigawatts of listed capacity. Luzerne County has nine proposals and 4.3 gigawatts of listed capacity. Three plants are listed in each of Carbon, Northampton and Schuylkill counties. Carbon County’s listed capacity is 350 megawatts, while Northampton and Schuylkill counties each have 1.2 gigawatts listed. Bradford, Monroe and Union counties each have two proposed plants. Listed capacity is 248 megawatts in Bradford County and 300 megawatts in Union County; no capacity figure was listed for Monroe County. One proposed plant is listed in each of Columbia, Lycoming, Montour and Wayne counties. The listed capacity figures total nearly 12.4 gigawatts in the counties where capacity was provided. The database listings may cover projects with different timelines and scopes than the statewide projections cited in PennEnvironment’s report. PennEnvironment says new gas plants can operate for 25 to 30 years and has called for a moratorium on new data centers, arguing that the projects could increase air pollution and long-term greenhouse-gas emissions. The organization’s conclusions and policy recommendations reflect its environmental advocacy position.
